Jio Platforms’ IPO grey market premium (GMP) stood at Rs 248, indicating a premium of 22.2%. The mainboard issue had a price band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share, with a total issue size of Rs 30,187.65 crore. The grey market premium is an unofficial indicator and does not guarantee the price at which shares will list on the stock exchanges.
08:54 (IST) Oct 28
Reliance JIO IPO listing: Jio Platforms eyes growth through AI, cloud computing and 6G technology
Jio Platforms is looking to expand beyond telecom, with technology, artificial intelligence and cloud computing expected to drive its next phase of growth, the telecom giant's managing director Akash Ambani told PTI earlier.
“There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology,” Ambani said, highlighting the company’s in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform, which serves 533.3 million customers.
The company is also exploring satellite connectivity and next-generation 6G technology as areas for future development. Ambani said Jio’s growth opportunities span mobile services, home broadband and digital solutions for enterprises.
He pointed to the scope for expansion, noting that around 26 crore Indians still use 2G services, while fixed broadband reaches only about 21% of households in the country.
08:45 (IST) Oct 28
JIO IPO listing: QIB portion subscribed 70.55 times
Qualified institutional buyers led the demand for Jio Platforms’ initial public offering, subscribing to their reserved portion 70.55 times. The non-institutional investor category was subscribed 14 times, while the retail investor portion was subscribed 2.72 times. The portions reserved for employees and Reliance Industries shareholders were subscribed around 2.93 times and 7.6 times, respectively. Overall, the IPO closed with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. The category-wise figures show the level of demand across institutional, non-institutional, retail, employee and shareholder segments during the issue’s three-day subscription window.
08:20 (IST) Oct 28
Jio IPO Listing: Mukesh Ambani’s plan to build an ‘everything company’
The listing of Jio Platforms furthers Mukesh Ambani’s plan to transform Reliance Industries from an oil-and-chemicals conglomerate into an “everything company” spanning consumer and technology businesses. Jio Platforms is Reliance Industries’ telecom and digital services unit and serves more than 530 million customers. Its initial public offering raised $3.2 billion and valued the company at up to $108.3 billion. The listing ceremony is expected to be attended by Akash Ambani, Mukesh Ambani’s eldest son and Jio Platforms’ managing director, according to an industry source with direct knowledge. The company’s stock market debut is scheduled for Wednesday, October 28.
08:10 (IST) Oct 28
Reliance Jio IPO: Reliance shares deliver around 900% returns in two decades
Over the last two decades, Reliance shares have delivered returns of around 900%, outperforming the benchmark Nifty index’s 685% return over the same period, according to LSEG data. Jio Platforms, the company’s telecom and digital services unit, is now set to make its stock market debut following its $3.2 billion IPO. The issue attracted strong demand, closing with subscriptions of 22.19 times the shares on offer. Jio Platforms is valued at up to $108.3 billion ahead of its listing on Wednesday, October 28.
07:58 (IST) Oct 28
Reliance Jio IPO: Investor demand build rapidly from day 1
Jio Platforms’ IPO was fully subscribed within the first 100 minutes of opening on October 21. The rapid response continued over the three-day bidding period, with the issue subscribed more than five times by Day 2 before closing at 22.19 times on October 23. In most Indian IPOs, subscription levels typically build gradually, with institutional investors often placing bids closer to the deadline. Jio Platforms’ offering saw substantial demand from the beginning of the subscription period. The issue was priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share, with a lot size of 12 shares.
07:49 (IST) Oct 28
JIO IPO listing: India ranks first by IPO deal count this year
India has become the world’s busiest initial public offering market this year by the number of deals, with 246 listings so far. However, it ranks fourth by the amount of money raised, at $13.5 billion, behind the United States, mainland China and Hong Kong, according to LSEG data.
Jio Platforms’ $3.2 billion offering is India’s largest IPO and attracted bids worth $77 billion. The listing is being closely watched as a test of investor appetite for large public offerings amid increased scrutiny of artificial intelligence-linked stocks. Several brokerages have described Jio Platforms’ $108.3 billion valuation as attractive, while flagging competition, heavy capital spending and changes in telecom rules as risks.
07:48 (IST) Oct 28
Reliance Jio IPO: ADIA, BlackRock and Fidelity among investors
Jio Platforms’ initial public offering received substantial demand from anchor investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, BlackRock and Fidelity. The $854 million worth of shares reserved for these investors received bids exceeding $25 billion on Monday, according to the provided inputs. The anchor investor response preceded the three-day public subscription period, during which the issue attracted around 1.3 crore applications. The $3.2 billion IPO was fully subscribed within its first 100 minutes and closed with overall subscriptions of 22.19 times. Total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports.
Jio IPO Listing: GMP indicates blockbuster 22% premium
Ahead of Jio Platforms’ stock market debut, the grey-market premium indicated potential listing gains of about 22%. The grey market is an unregulated market in which investors trade in shares before they are listed on the stock exchanges. The premium is an indication of the price at which unlisted shares are being traded relative to the IPO price. Jio Platforms’ issue was priced between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119 per share, with the upper end of the price band at Rs 1,119. However, the grey-market premium does not establish the actual listing price. The company’s market debut on Wednesday will determine its listing price.
07:47 (IST) Oct 28
Reliance Jio IPO: Jio IPO attracts around 1.3 crore applications
Jio Platforms’ initial public offering became the first public issue globally to receive more than one crore applications. The issue attracted around 1.3 crore applications, according to reports, as demand surged during the three-day bidding period. The $3.2 billion offering drew interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and shareholders. Subscription levels rose sharply after the IPO opened on October 21 and closed on October 23. The issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall, while total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports.
07:46 (IST) Oct 28
Jio IPO listing: Jio Platforms set for stock market debut
Jio Platforms, the telecom and digital services unit of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries, is set to list on the stock exchanges on October 28. The company’s $3.2 billion initial public offering has become India’s largest public issue, attracting strong interest from institutional and retail investors, employees and Reliance Industries shareholders. Jio Platforms is valued at up to $108.3 billion, potentially making it one of India’s biggest companies by market capitalisation when trading begins. The listing follows a three-day subscription period from October 21 to October 23, during which the issue was subscribed 22.19 times overall.
JIO IPO listing today: Mukesh Ambani-led Jio Platforms made a stellar debut on stock market today, October 28, after attracting unprecedented investor demand for its $3.2 billion initial public offering. Total demand, including the anchor investor portion, approached Rs 7.5 lakh crore, according to reports. Valued at up to $108.3 billion, the telecom and digital services company serves more than 530 million customers and has Meta and Google among its investors.

MLBx Mumbai is where America’s pastime meets India’s passion.
Cricket and baseball will square off this fall as MLBx heads to India. On October 24 at Mumbai Football Arena, Andheri Sports Complex, former MLB superstars Nick Swisher and Adrían González will take on India's T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav in a battle of power and defense supremacy. The game is a modified, co-ed 3-on-3 home run derby which rewards players for home runs and defensive catches - making it the perfect format for big leaguers and cricket stars to battle.
Each player will have one two-minute at-bat during a three-inning game, while the opposing team will set up their three players in the outfield. Teams earn a point for each home run and a point for each catch. Bonus points can be earned by hitting balls through a center-field target placed above the outfield fence or calling for a hot streak of five swings where offensive and defensive points count double. title: In 2018, Antipodes Island was declared free of invasive mice; eight years later, scientists reported ground beetle numbers 40 times higher, with rove beetles up more than 20-fold after predator removal
raw_text:
When conservation teams confirmed in 2018 that invasive house mice had been removed from Antipodes Island, it marked the end of one of New Zealand’s most ambitious island restoration efforts. The remote subantarctic island had carried mice for more than a century, and their appetite for insects, seeds, plants and occasionally bird eggs had quietly reshaped the ecosystem. Eight years on, scientists have reported that ground beetle numbers are now about 40 times higher than before the mice were removed, while rove beetles have increased more than twentyfold. The findings, published in Conservation Science and Practice, offer a rare long-term measure of what happens when a relentless predator disappears from a small island ecosystem. They also show that ecological recovery is not always immediate, tidy or predictable, but it can be remarkably powerful when the pressure is finally lifted. Read more details about it here:
A remote island under pressure
Antipodes Island lies in New Zealand’s subantarctic region, a wild and windswept place valued for its seabird colonies, endemic land birds and distinctive invertebrate life. The main island is home to species found nowhere else, including the Antipodes Island snipe, Antipodes parakeet and Reischek’s parakeet. For decades, however, house mice were part of the island’s ecological reality. They arrived through human activity and became established despite the island’s isolation and harsh climate.
Their impact was not subtle. Research before the eradication found that mice preyed heavily on surface-dwelling invertebrates, including beetles, spiders and other ground-active animals. 
Scientists also noted that mice competed with native birds for food and altered plant and seed dynamics. In short, the mice were not merely another animal on the island. They were an introduced predator whose presence influenced much of the food web beneath the more visible birdlife.
The Department of Conservation Te Papa Atawhai describes the removal operation as the Million Dollar Mouse campaign. In the winter of 2016, a 13-strong team used helicopters to spread cereal bait containing the rodent toxin brodifacoum across the main island in two applications. Monitoring followed in February 2018, when teams deployed 200 inked tracking tunnels and searched for three weeks with rodent detection dogs. No mice were detected, confirming that the eradication had succeeded.
What the new research found
Representative image
The latest study examined how the island’s invertebrate communities responded in the years after mouse removal. Its headline result is striking: ground beetle abundance was reported to be roughly 40 times higher than before eradication, while rove beetle numbers had risen by more than 20 times. These are not small statistical shifts. They represent a major recovery among animals that sit close to the base of the island’s terrestrial food web.
Beetles matter because they are more than a food source for birds. Ground beetles and rove beetles help process organic material, move through soil and litter layers, and form part of the predator and prey networks that keep island ecosystems functioning. When mice were present, these insects faced constant predation pressure. Once that pressure was removed, populations could rebuild across multiple breeding cycles. The new findings suggest that the recovery was not a brief rebound but a sustained ecological change.
The result also fits earlier monitoring. A related study reported that invertebrate groups preyed upon by mice increased between two and 35 times after eradication, with pitfall trapping proving especially useful for ground-active animals such as beetles and spiders. The newer figures for ground and rove beetles show that some groups have continued to climb well beyond the early recovery phase.
Why beetles make good messengers
Large animals often dominate conservation headlines, but invertebrates can provide some of the clearest evidence that an ecosystem is healing. They generally have short life cycles, so their populations can respond quickly when conditions improve. On Antipodes Island, this makes beetles valuable indicators of change. If mice were still suppressing insect life, the beetles would be unlikely to show such dramatic increases.
Their recovery also has consequences further up the food chain. Native birds such as snipe and pipits depend on invertebrates, and earlier post-eradication surveys found that both species more than doubled after mice were removed. More insects and other invertebrates can mean more food for birds, particularly during breeding season when energy demands are high. In this way, the beetle boom is not simply a victory for beetles. It is evidence that the island’s ecological machinery is beginning to work with fewer human-caused interruptions.
There is an important lesson here about patience. Conservation projects often celebrate the day a pest is declared eradicated, and understandably so. But the real measure of success may arrive years later, when native species have had time to reproduce, disperse and reclaim ecological roles. Antipodes Island shows why long-term monitoring matters. Without repeated surveys, scientists might have underestimated how deeply mouse predation had affected the island and how substantial the response could become.
Recovery is not restoration
The beetle finds are encouraging, but that doesn’t mean Antipodes Island has just gone back to some pristine, original state. Ecosystems change with time, and recovery from an invasion can lead to new patterns rather than a perfect copy of the past. Some species may bounce back faster than others. Some may expand into areas they once avoided. Others may remain limited by habitat, climate or the availability of other resources.
That complexity is part of what makes the study valuable. Rather than treating the island as a simple before-and-after experiment, the research helps scientists understand which parts of the ecosystem respond most strongly to predator removal. Beetles were clearly among the major beneficiaries. Their dramatic increase suggests that mice had been holding back populations for a long time, possibly preventing some species from reaching the abundance their habitat could otherwise support.
It is also a reminder that eradications can have consequences beyond the target species. The Antipodes operation used a toxin that required careful planning because of possible risks to non-target wildlife. Conservation managers had to balance the damage caused by mice against the potential exposure of native birds and other animals to bait. The eventual success of the project reflects both the technical difficulty of the operation and the importance of rigorous monitoring afterwards.
A signal for island conservation worldwide
Antipodes Island is remote, but its story has relevance far beyond the Southern Ocean. Islands are especially vulnerable to invasive mammals because native species often evolve without defences against predators such as rodents. When mice, rats or cats arrive, they can rapidly alter food webs, prey on nesting birds and reduce invertebrate populations. Removing those invaders can therefore create unusually clear opportunities for recovery.
The Antipodes results add to a growing body of evidence that pest eradication can deliver measurable ecological gains. Earlier monitoring already documented rebounds in native birds, including snipe and pipits, after mice disappeared. The beetle data now reveal recovery at a less visible but equally important level of the ecosystem. Together, these findings show that conservation action can benefit entire food webs, not only the species people most easily notice.
Eight years after the mice were declared gone, the Antipodes Island has a quiet but powerful message. Sometimes the best evidence of ecological repair is not the return of the single charismatic animal but the return of the small creatures that lived in the shadows. In this case, the beetles have made themselves impossible to ignore.

title: A Connecticut couple has committed $410 million to turn a 125-acre former coal and oil power plant into a waterfront park; zoning approval moves the long-closed industrial site closer to public use
raw_text:
For decades, a stretch of Norwalk’s waterfront was defined by smokestacks, industrial machinery and the imposing presence of a coal- and oil-burning power plant. Now, the same 125-acre peninsula overlooking Long Island Sound is poised for a radically different future. A $410 million investment from Connecticut couple Austin and Allison McChord is helping transform the former industrial site into Manresa Wilds, a public-facing destination built around open space, recreation and carefully managed cultural events.
A major step for Manresa Wilds
According to the Hartford Courant and CT Mirror, Norwalk’s Planning and Zoning Commission unanimously approved a special zoning district covering the proposed Manresa Wilds development.
The decision establishes the framework under which the McChords and their development team can continue refining plans for the site. The project is expected to combine parkland with amenities including walking trails, live music, private events, boat rentals and a restaurant or brewpub.
The $410 million commitment includes the environmental remediation required to address the site's industrial legacy. However, the zoning decision does not represent the final approval for every element of the development. 
Future phases will require additional zoning reviews, detailed planning and traffic studies before construction can move forward.
From industrial site to public destination
The scale of the transformation is particularly striking because the property spent decades serving as a power-generation facility. The long-closed plant's buildings are now being incorporated into a broader vision that aims to give the waterfront a new public purpose.
The first stage, known as the Northern Forest, is already under construction. As reported by the Hartford Courant and CT Mirror, the phase includes walking trails, open fields and outdoor classrooms and is expected to open next year.
A later phase is expected to focus on the adaptive reuse of the former power plant's turbine hall and administration building. That portion of the project is currently targeted for completion in 2032.
Community concerns reshape the plans
The redevelopment has not been without controversy. Nearby residents raised concerns about increased traffic, noise and the potential disruption caused by events at the site. More than 200 residents signed a petition opposing the proposed special zoning district and calling for a scaled-back approach.
According to CT Mirror and the Hartford Courant, in response, the Manresa Wilds team conducted community meetings and collected more than 4,000 comments about the plans.
Several changes followed. Plans for a hotel were removed, outdoor lighting was reduced and parking was capped at 200 spaces, with access managed through a reservation system.
The approved zoning framework also places limits on events. No more than four monthly events can accommodate between 150 and 400 guests, while events drawing as many as 800 people will be restricted to four annually. On days when multiple activities take place, total attendance will be capped at 1,000.
Preserving the past while opening the waterfront
The project seeks to balance public access with the site's industrial heritage. Its redevelopment could eventually turn an inaccessible piece of Norwalk's waterfront into a destination combining nature, education, recreation and historic architecture.
While concerns over traffic and neighborhood impact remain, the zoning approval marks a significant milestone. For a peninsula once associated with power generation, Manresa Wilds represents an ambitious attempt to give an industrial landscape an entirely new life—one shaped around public space and the waterfront rather than power production.

title: Michael Dell says Trump Account 'moment has become a movement'; shares donations from Silicon Valley and beyond; names include SpaceX COO
raw_text:
Michael Dell has hailed the Trump Accounts program as a growing national movement. Dell CEO took to social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) to share the details of fresh contributions from Silicon Valley and beyond. In a reaction pots, Dell wrote, “This is how a moment becomes a movement.” For those unaware, this initiative is designed to give every American child under 18 a stake in the stock market. It has already opened 9 million accounts and is on track to auto-create accounts for all 70 million children using Social Security data.
Contributions made by SpaceX COO, Ray Dalio and others
Dell's post highlighted a growing list of high-profile donors stepping up to fund Trump Accounts, the tax-deferred investment savings program for American children under 18. Among the names: Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner, who is contributing $250 each to Trump Accounts for more than 140,000 children in Indiana, and hedge fund manager Ray Dalio and his wife Barbara, who are extending similar $250 contributions to children across Connecticut.
The biggest single commitment by dollar value came from SpaceX President and COO Gwynne Shotwell, who — along with her husband, Robert — is donating one share of SpaceX stock to each of more than 2 million children, a gift Dell's post pegs at roughly $325 million. 
The donation is specifically targeted at children between the ages of 11 and 17 in lower-income communities, continuing a pattern Shotwell set earlier this year when she first announced the gift shortly after SpaceX's record-breaking public listing.
Dell used the post to personally thank Gerstner for organizing the broader donor push through Invest America, crediting him for turning the concept into reality, and thanked every donor who has stepped up to participate.

title: Prince William inherited the $1.3 billion Duchy of Cornwall, spanning 128,000 acres, after Queen Elizabeth II’s death; earning $31 million annually from it, he now plans to sell 20% to fund housing and green projects
raw_text:
Prince William is using one of the British royal family's most valuable assets to pursue causes close to his heart, with plans to sell a portion of his vast estate to fund housing, environmental recovery and renewable energy projects.
The 
Prince of Wales
, 44, took control of the Duchy of Cornwall after the death of his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, in September 2022. The estate, which spans more than 128,000 acres, is valued at over $1.3 billion and provides William with an annual private income of nearly $31 million.
However, the future king is looking beyond the traditional role of the estate as a source of income. According to a report by The Times, William plans to sell around 20% of the Duchy's assets, potentially raising an estimated $670 million to support a new approach centred on social needs, nature recovery and clean energy.
Why Prince William wants to reshape the Duchy of Cornwall
Established in 1337, the Duchy of Cornwall was created to provide an income for the heir to the British throne and support the household and public responsibilities associated with the role. It has traditionally consisted of land, property and other assets managed on behalf of the heir apparent.
William inherited control of the estate when his father, King Charles III, became monarch following Queen Elizabeth II's death. 
When William eventually becomes king, control will pass to his eldest son, Prince George, continuing the centuries-old tradition.
Under William's leadership, however, the estate is being encouraged to take a more active role in addressing local challenges. The reported plan to sell a fifth of its assets would allow it to focus its resources on five key areas, including Cornwall, Dartmoor, the Isles of Scilly, Bath and parts of London.
Duchy chief executive Will Bax has outlined a vision in which the organisation evaluates its presence according to the positive impact it can deliver.
"If we don’t see an opportunity for positive impact, then perhaps we don’t need to be a part of that place," Bax told The Times.
"But where there is social need and where there is environmental challenge and where there is an opportunity to enable change, then we’ll be a great partner in working with people to achieve that."
The approach reflects William's broader interest in using his position and resources to address social and environmental concerns.
Tackling homelessness through housing projects
The 128,000-acre Duchy of Cornwall is valued at $1.3 billion and provides Prince William with nearly $31 million in annual income. (Photo: Getty)
One of William's priorities for the Duchy is addressing homelessness, an issue he has also made central to his wider Homewards initiative.
The project seeks to develop practical, locally driven solutions to homelessness, bringing together organisations and communities to explore ways of preventing people from losing their homes.
In 2024, Ben Murphy, estate director at the Duchy of Cornwall, explained that William had asked the estate to address homelessness in Cornwall and other areas where it operates.
"As one of his key priorities for the Duchy of Cornwall, Prince William asked us to address the homelessness challenge within Cornwall and other areas where the estate resides," Murphy said.
The Duchy is already developing social housing in Nansledan, near Newquay in Cornwall. The project is part of a broader effort to create communities that combine housing with local services and commercial spaces.
Another planned development on Market Street in Newquay aims to create a new high street featuring independent businesses, local artisans and community enterprises. The project is expected to be completed in 2028 and is intended to help strengthen the local economy.
These developments illustrate how the estate's property portfolio could be used to support communities beyond its traditional financial role.
Why William is redirecting money from Dartmoor Prison
The Prince of Wales has also taken steps to redirect income from an estate asset that is no longer being used for its original purpose.
Dartmoor Prison, which has remained empty since July 2024, had generated approximately $2 million a year in rental income for William. Rather than continue to retain that money, he directed that the annual amount be returned to the local community through the Princetown Community Fund.
According to a September press release, the fund will support projects delivering lasting social, economic and environmental benefits for people in Princetown and the surrounding Dartmoor area.
The decision aligns with the wider direction of the Duchy under William: ensuring that assets and income are connected to the needs of the communities in which the estate operates.
Princess Kate's early childhood initiative finds a partner in the Duchy
William's plans also intersect with the work of his wife, Princess Kate, particularly her focus on early childhood development and the role of nature in children's well-being.
Kate's Centre for Early Childhood has partnered with the Duchy of Cornwall to explore how time spent outdoors can support the mental well-being and development of young children, as well as the people who care for them.
The collaboration, launched in Nansledan, examines how nature, creativity and relationships can help children develop the social and emotional skills that contribute to lifelong health and well-being.
"This project is about exploring how nature, creativity and relationships can best support the healthy development of babies and young children," Kate said in a video.
"We believe that taking a whole-child approach is important, and nature becomes a wonderful place to explore how we can successfully nurture the social and emotional skills that underpin lifelong health and wellbeing."
The initiative connects the Duchy's environmental ambitions with Kate's long-standing interest in the early years of childhood, highlighting how the estate's land can be used for projects that benefit families and local communities.
Cornwall remains important to William and his family
Beyond its financial significance and public initiatives, the Duchy of Cornwall also holds a place in Prince William and Kate’s family life.
Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly are among the destinations where the family spends time together. The Prince and Princess of Wales have also shared photographs and videos of their children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, taken in Cornwall as part of their birthday celebrations this year.

title: 'Keeping a list of names': Abhishek Banerjee warns cops trying to 'please' Suvendu
raw_text:
Banerjee alleged that several police officers had been targeting TMC workers to secure favourable postings
NEW DELHi: Trinamool Congress (TMC) national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee on Thursday warned police officers allegedly targeting party workers to please West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari. He added that those responsible would face consequences when his party returned to power.“I am keeping a list of names. None will be spared once the government changes,” Banerjee said, accusing police officers of implicating thousands of TMC workers in false cases at the behest of the chief minister.
“I will identify the names of the police officers who are acting at his (Adhikari's) behest. I will record their names. Those who are trying to please the chief minister and secure good postings will see the consequences in two years,” he said.
Banerjee alleged that several police officers had been targeting TMC workers to secure favourable postings and warned that their actions would be scrutinised if the party returned to power. He also accused an IPS officer in Paschim Medinipur of targeting TMC workers despite having earlier congratulated him on the party's expected electoral victory.
The remarks come amid a political confrontation between the ruling BJP and the TMC following the arrest of former West Bengal minister Indranil Sen over alleged financial irregularities linked to Durga Puja preview shows and the sale of passes.
Adhikari has alleged that Sen may not have been the sole beneficiary of the suspected irregularities, claiming that the investigation could reach more prominent political figures, including former chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He has maintained that the law would take its course regardless of the influence of those under investigation.Hitting back at the BJP over Sen's arrest, Abhishek Banerjee alleged that people who refused to compromise their conscience were being jailed, while those accused of serious offences were spared after joining the saffron party.The case centres on alleged irregularities involving MassArt Society, which investigators suspect collected money between 2022 and 2025 through passes for privileged entry to Durga Puja pandals and preview shows while creating a false impression of an association with UNESCO. The organisation's financial transactions and the use of the funds collected are under investigation.

title: Spain train tragedy: Glitch, 3 operator errors behind crash that killed 68
raw_text:
A technical glitch followed by a series of alleged human errors at a railway control centre may have led to a devastating collision between two high-speed trains in Spain, killing 68.
According to Spanish news outlet El Diario, the incident began around 8.30am on Wednesday when a computer malfunction knocked out the LZB train control system on a 69-km stretch of track. The failure automatically stopped several trains, including an Iryo service and a state-owned Renfe AVE train travelling behind it.
However, instead of requiring the AVE train to proceed at a restricted speed, the control centre at Madrid's Atocha station allegedly instructed its driver to resume the journey at normal speed. The train was travelling at high speed when it struck the stationary Iryo train from behind at around 8.53am near Urda, in central Spain.
El Diario, citing audio recordings of conversations between train drivers and the control centre, reported that the operator appeared to have authorised the resumption of services without applying the necessary safety precautions. The recordings raised questions about whether the operator had misread the relevant protocol and failed to account for the position of the Iryo train.
When the LZB system is unavailable, railway procedures require trains to operate under trackside signalling, with drivers proceeding at sight speed. According to El Diario, industry sources said this means travelling at no more than 40 kmph, allowing drivers to react to obstructions ahead. A high-speed train travelling at around 200 kmph, by contrast, can require more than a kilometre to stop.
The report also highlighted a second missed opportunity to prevent the collision. About five minutes after the AVE train was authorised to resume its journey, the Iryo driver contacted the control centre to report that her train remained stopped because of the signalling problem. She was also told to continue at normal speed once able to do so.
Despite the communication, there was no indication in the recordings that the control centre warned the AVE driver about the stationary train ahead. The AVE travelled approximately 25 km before the collision.
Transport minister Óscar Puente described the decision to allow the AVE train to resume at normal speed as “inexplicable”. The investigation by the Civil Guard and Spain's Railway Accident Investigation Commission is expected to establish how the technical failure and decisions at the control centre contributed to the disaster.
The crash is Spain's second deadly high-speed rail accident this year, following a January collision that killed 46 people. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has pledged a full investigation and improvements to restore public confidence in the country's rail network.

title: Patrick Mahomes’ retirement timeline takes a surprising turn as Chiefs trainer reveals his 10 Super Bowl goal
raw_text:
Patrick Mahomes has a big goal for his NFL career, and it could decide when he finally walks away from football. His longtime trainer, Jeff Christensen, says the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback once told him that he would consider retiring after winning 10 Super Bowls. Mahomes has already won three championships, but according to Christensen, his focus remains on becoming the greatest quarterback in NFL history rather than making more money.
Jeff Christensen explains Patrick Mahomes’ retirement plan and 10 Super Bowl goal
Speaking on 
Fearless with Jason Whitlock
 on Thursday, Christensen shared a conversation he had with Mahomes when the quarterback was a rookie in 2017. He asked the young player about his “get out” number, meaning the point at which he would feel ready to leave football behind.
Christensen explained that some players claim money does not matter to them, but their attitude toward the game can change after they sign big contracts. Mahomes, however, gave him an answer that stood out.
“Patrick said, ‘My get out is the wins when I win my 10th Super Bowl,’” Christensen recalled.
The answer showed that Mahomes had set a clear target for his career from an early age. Instead of naming a salary or a financial goal that would convince him to retire, he pointed to winning championships. 
His trainer believes that ambition has continued to guide his choices as his career has moved forward.
Christensen also remembered telling Mahomes in July 2017 that he had the ability to become the greatest quarterback ever. He said he saw something special in the young player and later shared that view with Matt Kafka before the Chiefs traded Alex Smith.
“He just had it,” Christensen said.
He also praised Mahomes for staying true to what he said he wanted to achieve. “He does not care about money. He wants to be the greatest. And so his action plan is exactly on schedule.”
Christensen’s comments describe how he sees Mahomes’ approach to football, rather than confirming when the quarterback will retire. Mahomes has not announced a retirement date, and winning 10 Super Bowls remains a goal, not a confirmed outcome.
Patrick Mahomes has three Super Bowl wins as Chiefs quarterback
Mahomes has already won three Super Bowls with Kansas City and earned three Super Bowl MVP awards. His first championship came in Super Bowl LIV, when the Chiefs defeated the San Francisco 49ers. He later led Kansas City to further titles, building a record that puts him among the most successful quarterbacks of his era.
He also became the youngest quarterback to win both the regular-season MVP award and the Super Bowl MVP award in the same season, achieving the feat during the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIV campaign.
However, his latest career goal comes as Kansas City works through challenges on the field. Mahomes recently addressed reports of a disagreement with offensive lineman Josh Simmons during a team meeting with head coach Andy Reid. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, he said the situation had not taken his attention away from the team’s work.
“Stuff like that doesn’t really bother me because I’m so in the moment, in the team,” Mahomes said. “We’ve had the right conversations now. We’re moving in the right direction.”
Mahomes also explained why difficult discussions can matter inside a team. “You have to be able to have tough conversations so that you can have better conversations going forward,” he said.
Simmons has not played this season because of a back issue, while undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson has started in his absence. Simmons could return from injured reserve in Week 11 against the Arizona Cardinals on November 22.

title: Harmanpreet, Sukhjeet score braces as India beat China 5-2 at Asian Champions Trophy
raw_text:
Captain 
Harmanpreet Singh
 and forward 
Sukhjeet Singh
 struck twice each as India continued their winning run at the Asian Champions Trophy, defeating a spirited China 5-2 in front of the home crowd at the Olympian Surjit Singh Hockey Stadium on Thursday.
India, who had opened their campaign with a commanding 13-0 win over Bangladesh, had to work harder against a youthful Chinese side but eventually secured their second consecutive victory. Harmanpreet converted two penalty corners, while Sukhjeet scored twice from open play. Jugraj Singh added the fifth goal with another successful set-piece conversion.
China, despite their defeat, showed resilience and threatened India at different stages, with Peng Yang and Chongcong Chen scoring from penalty corners. However, the hosts' attacking quality and ability to capitalise on crucial opportunities proved decisive.
Sukhjeet breaks the deadlock as China put up a fight
India dominated possession and made repeated circle entries from the opening whistle but struggled to create clear-cut chances in the early stages. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 13th minute when Jugraj produced a superb scoop from deep to find Sukhjeet inside the Chinese circle. The forward controlled the ball brilliantly before lifting it over goalkeeper Huanyu Wu.
China earned their first penalty corner in the 18th minute, but India's defence held firm. The hosts then won two successive penalty corners in the 20th minute, only for Harmanpreet to miss the target with his second attempt.
The young Chinese side continued to frustrate India's attacks and drew level in the 26th minute. Peng Yang converted their second penalty corner with a drag-flick past goalkeeper Krishan Bahadur Pathak.
India responded almost immediately. A minute later, Harmanpreet restored the hosts' lead with a powerful, low flick from their third penalty corner to make it 2-1.
China earned two more penalty corners in the closing stages of the first half but failed to convert either, allowing India to carry a narrow advantage into the break.
Harmanpreet, Sukhjeet extend India's lead
India began the second half on the front foot, and Harmanpreet struck again in the 31st minute, converting another penalty corner with a grounded flick to give the hosts a 3-1 cushion.
Three minutes later, Sukhjeet completed his brace. The forward finished off a pass from Aditya Arjun Lalage after the latter controlled an aerial ball from Harmanpreet near the halfway line.
China refused to surrender and reduced the deficit in the 36th minute. Chongcong Chen converted their fourth penalty corner with a well-executed variation, bringing the score to 4-2 and keeping the visitors in contention.
India continued to press for more goals. Jugraj saw one of his penalty-corner attempts saved by Wu, but the defender made amends in the 47th minute, unleashing a powerful, grounded flick from a set piece to restore India's three-goal advantage.
The hosts earned another penalty corner two minutes before the final hooter, but Harmanpreet's effort was kept out by the Chinese goalkeeper. India, however, had done enough to seal a comfortable 5-2 victory.
India face Japan next
The win gives India a second successive victory in the tournament following their emphatic opening-day triumph over Bangladesh. China, meanwhile, are still searching for their first win after losing 4-5 to Asian Games silver medallists Malaysia on Tuesday.
India will next face Japan on Friday, while China take on South Korea as the tournament continues.

title: 'Don't push us': SC warns of harsh stand on firecrackers if orders go unenforced
raw_text:
As Delhi-NCR braces for Diwali celebrations, concerns over firecracker emissions and worsening air pollution put the spotlight on the festival’s environmental cost.
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it was not inclined to impose a complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but warned authorities against pushing it to take a "very harsh stand" by failing to enforce its orders on the ground.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale said repeated judicial directions would serve little purpose unless authorities ensured compliance, stressing that air pollution affected "every living being"."We are not inclined to completely ban but don’t push us to take a very harsh stand," the bench said as reported by news agency PTI. The Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati outlined measures taken by the Delhi government and the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to tackle pollution.“There is no point in passing orders and directions unless you give effect to them on the ground, otherwise, it becomes a mockery,” the bench observed.The court said the matter was not adversarial and called for serious action and cooperation from all stakeholders to regulate the use of firecrackers.“Every year we are trying to balance it out but unless there is cooperation from everyone, it can’t be done,” the bench said, adding that the concerned officers must be present on the ground to monitor implementation.
The bench also suggested roping in prominent personalities, including sportspersons, to spread public awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers.Bhati told the court that the Delhi government had drawn up an extensive plan to tackle the pollution season. Measures scheduled to come into effect from November include curbs on older vehicles and construction and demolition activities, along with staggered office timings.
The Centre informed the court that internal consultations on the use of barium in firecrackers were still under way. Bhati sought three weeks to complete the process, and the bench said it would consider the issue after that period.The Supreme Court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case on air pollution in the National Capital Region covering firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management. The other petition seeks a ban on the manufacture of firecrackers.

title: The political obituary can wait: Lula, Bibi and the art of survival
raw_text:
One is a Left-wing icon challenging Trump's dominance of Latin America. The other is a Right-wing nationalist who helped persuade the US president to attack Iran. Yet, despite their ideological differences, Lula and Netanyahu have shown why writing political obituaries can be a dangerous business.
Opposite poles, one instinct
They could hardly be further apart. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, leads Latin America's biggest left-wing party. 
Benjamin Netanyahu
, 77, heads the most right-wing government in Israel's history and is Donald Trump's closest ally abroad. One has spent the year denouncing American power in his hemisphere. The other spent it pulling American power into his.
No side has reached a majority mark in the Israeli elections.
Yet within a span of three days, both did what their critics thought they could not. Lula came from behind to win a fourth term on October 25. Two days later, Netanyahu turned an election night that the exit polls called a rout into something closer to a draw.
Both have given master classes in the oldest skill in politics: Staying alive.
Interestingly, US President Donald Trump had a stake in both contests. He openly endorsed Netanyahu, and he has long counted the Bolsonaro family as friends. His scoreline is 1-1.
Lula: The comeback that stalled the Donroe Doctrine
Brazil's first round on October 4 looked like the end. Flavio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of the jailed former president, took about 47% of the valid vote to Lula's 45%, defying final polls that had the president ahead. Lula admitted he had expected to win outright. The first survey afterwards gave Bolsonaro a six-point runoff lead.
Three weeks later, the official count gave Lula 51.79% to 48.21%. The result halted a right-wing wave that had already delivered victories for Jose Antonio Kast in Chile, Abelardo de la Espriella in Colombia and Keiko Fujimori in Peru.
How did he do it? Lula went back to the streets and went after the Bolsonaro family directly, raising its alleged links to militias. Flávio had greeted his first-round lead by proclaiming the end of the Workers' Party era. It proved premature.
Lula won the Brazil elections with over 4 million votes
Trump's "Donroe Doctrine", his muscular update of the Monroe Doctrine, has split the hemisphere into friends and foes since the US seized Nicolas Maduro in January. Brazil was its biggest prize. Flavio had promised to join the US-backed Americas Shield security pact and to free his father. Lula has halted the Trump wagon. He is now the most powerful leftist still standing in Washington's way.
The defeat has since turned into a spectacle. Flavio crossed into Argentina before flying to Miami with his family, after Trump offered them a way out. From the United States, he now casts himself as a victim of political persecution. Lula, meanwhile, is pressing ahead with his agenda.
Netanyahu: Written off, not counted out
In Israel, the script ran the other way. Almost every pre-election poll put Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc in front. When voting closed on October 27, the broadcasters' exit polls showed Eisenkot ahead by two or three seats, and his supporters partied in Tel Aviv.
The count told another story. With about 90% of ballots tallied, Likud is the largest party with 26 seats, and Netanyahu's right-wing and religious bloc holds 53 seats to Eisenkot's 48.
Turnout hit a historic high. Arab Israelis voted in record numbers, while Netanyahu's own base came out to defend him. Likud's response was telling: It accused the Arab parties of stealing the election. Trump, for his part, claimed his endorsement had turned the tide and hailed a come-from-behind performance.
Let’s be clear:
 This is not an outright victory for Netanyahu. His bloc is eight seats short of a majority and down from 68 in the outgoing Knesset. But the opposition's arithmetic is worse. Arab parties won a record 19 seats, enough to give the anti-Netanyahu camp a majority, yet every Zionist opposition party except the Democrats has ruled out relying on them.
Roughly 450,000 absentee ballots remain, official results are due on November 4, and coalition talks could drag on for months. If they fail, a unity government or yet another election both leave Netanyahu in office. Until then he stays on as caretaker, with full war powers, as a renewed war with Iran looms.
The majority mark in Israel is 61
Netanyahu is already playing for time. He has assured his far-right partners. President Isaac Herzog has urged the parties to avoid another election and keep an open mind, while Washington says it has not decided whether to weigh in.
What survivors share
The two leaders from the opposite spectrum share a toolkit. Both have come back from the dead before: Lula from 580 days in prison, Netanyahu from defeats in 1999 and 2021 and a corruption trial that has shadowed him since 2020. Both turned Trump into fuel. Lula wrapped himself in sovereignty against American tariffs and threats; Netanyahu wore Trump's endorsement, which the US president now claims turned the tide.
Both also owe something to opponents who could not close the deal. Flavio Bolsonaro let a two-point lead slip away in three weeks. Eisenkot's camp has an anti-Netanyahu majority in the new Knesset but no agreed way to use it.
The art of survival
The twin results say something about the moment. Voters on both continents are angry, yet anger has not produced clean breaks. Leaders with deep networks and long memories still know how to bring their people to the polls, and how to make rivals pay for hesitation.
Lula's fight is over; he will be sworn in on January 1, 2027. Netanyahu's is not, and he may yet lose the coalition game. But no one should hurry to write his political obituary.

title: US intelligence confirms image shows China's secret spaceplane in orbit; design resembles X-37B
raw_text:
The US Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) has confirmed that a satellite image released in a newly declassified report shows China's experimental reusable spaceplane in orbit, offering a clearer view of a spacecraft whose design closely resembles the US Space Force's X-37B.
The higher-resolution image, captured by a satellite operated by Maxar Technologies, now known as Vantor, was included in the DIA's latest unclassified assessment of security challenges in space, released on October 26. Although a lower-resolution version had circulated publicly since 2024, the spacecraft's identity had not been confirmed at the time.
The image shows a compact, shuttle-like vehicle with wings, twin vertical tails, an open payload bay and a rear-mounted module with solar panels deployed on either side. Its overall configuration resembles the X-37B, an uncrewed reusable spaceplane operated by the US Space Force, although the Chinese vehicle appears to have longer wings.
“A key capability for reusable space activities are spaceplanes like this PRC [People’s Republic of China] Spaceplane captured by Maxar. Spaceplanes can launch into orbit to place objects in space or even test them and return to earth [sic],” reads the caption to the picture in DIA’s report.
The exact date and circumstances of the satellite's observation have not been publicly disclosed in the DIA report. However, the image carries a 2024 copyright date, placing it within the period when China's spacecraft was conducting its third orbital mission.
China has conducted four spaceplane missions since 2020
China is understood to have conducted four orbital missions using its experimental reusable spaceplane since 2020. The latest mission began on February 7, 2026, and the spacecraft remained in orbit as of the latest available reports.
The vehicle's activities have attracted attention because it has reportedly released smaller objects into orbit and carried out operations involving other spacecraft. During its third mission, which lasted from December 14, 2023, to September 6, 2024, the spaceplane was observed releasing multiple smaller objects. Their identities and purposes remain unknown.
Analysis of open-source orbital tracking data by astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell also indicated that the spacecraft involved in the latest mission released and subsequently recaptured a smaller object during a series of orbital operations. These activities point to its ability to interact with objects in space, although its precise mission objectives remain undisclosed.
The spacecraft is commonly referred to as Shenlong in Western reports, but its official designation and the model shown in the image have not been definitively established.
The DIA report states that “China has two primary spaceplane models: the Shenlong and Tengyun,” without specifying which one appears in the photograph.
China's Shenlong programme has been discussed publicly since at least 2007, when images emerged of what was believed to be a prototype or test vehicle mounted beneath an H-6 bomber. Separately, the state-run China Aerospace Science and Industry Corporation unveiled its Tengyun reusable spaceplane concept in 2016. The proposed system was designed around a two-stage-to-orbit approach involving a carrier aircraft, rather than relying entirely on a conventional rocket launch.
It remains unclear whether the planned Tengyun test targeted for 2025 took place.
How China's spaceplane compares with the US X-37B
The Chinese vehicle shares several visible design features with the US Space Force's X-37B, including a winged body, payload bay and a configuration intended to support a return to Earth. Both spacecraft are uncrewed and designed for reusable orbital operations.
The US has built two X-37B vehicles, which have flown a total of eight orbital missions since 2010. The spacecraft can carry experiments and payloads into orbit before returning to Earth for recovery and refurbishment. Much of its operational activity remains classified.
China's spaceplane is also understood to launch aboard a conventional rocket before operating in orbit and returning to Earth for a runway landing. A secretive Chinese airbase in the country's northwest, featuring an exceptionally long runway, has been identified in reporting as a possible landing site for the vehicle, although the full details of its recovery operations remain unclear.
The image does not establish whether the Chinese spacecraft carries weapons or is being used for offensive missions. However, its ability to manoeuvre, deploy objects and potentially interact with other spacecraft has raised questions about the military applications of reusable spaceplanes.
DIA warns of growing competition in space
The DIA's report places reusable spaceplanes within a wider assessment of expanding space capabilities and the potential risks they pose to US and allied assets.
In general, “spaceplanes are … reusable and feature enhanced maneuverability, making them more suitable for certain missions than traditional satellites,” DIA’s report notes.
Such vehicles can potentially deploy small satellites, conduct experiments, inspect other spacecraft and return payloads to Earth. Their ability to alter trajectories and approach other objects also makes them useful for missions that conventional satellites may find more difficult to perform.
The report also discusses China's development of counterspace capabilities, including ground-based laser weapons that could disrupt, degrade or damage satellites in low Earth orbit.
“China has multiple ground-based laser weapons with varying power levels to disrupt, degrade, or damage satellites in LEO,” the DIA said. “By the late 2020s, China may field space-based directed energy systems and higher-powered ground-based directed energy systems capable of threatening satellites in higher orbits.”
The assessment also points to China's testing of ground-based anti-satellite missiles, satellite servicing and refuelling technologies, and robotic systems that could potentially interact with spacecraft in orbit.
China has expanded its space-based intelligence and surveillance capabilities in recent years, while the United States and Russia are also developing systems that can manoeuvre close to other satellites. Such activities have raised concerns about the potential for interference with, or attacks on, space assets.
The DIA report also explains the economic rationale behind reusable technology, noting that conventional space access has relied heavily on expendable launch vehicles and spacecraft.
“In general, access to space traditionally requires expendable spacecraft: single-use launch vehicles, satellites, and one-time use capsules designed to maximize performance. Reliance on expendable vehicles has made access to space expensive and exclusive,” DIA’s report explains. “Reusable technologies, while even more difficult and expensive to develop and build, stand to greatly reduce the cost of spaceflight by recovering, refurbishing, and reusing rocket stages, fairings, and capsules.”
The newly released image provides a clearer look at China's experimental spaceplane, but its full capabilities, payloads and intended military role remain unknown. Its resemblance to the X-37B, combined with reported orbital manoeuvres and object deployments, underscores the growing role of reusable spacecraft in the increasingly competitive space domain.

title: 'Turn the blade inward': Xi swings the axe again, expels 33 in major CCP purge
raw_text:
Chinese President 
Xi Jinping
 has intensified his sweeping anti-corruption campaign, with the Communist Party expelling 33 members, including senior military officers and prominent political figures, as a key leadership meeting exposed the scale of the ongoing purge.
The expulsions were confirmed in a communique issued on Thursday at the end of a four-day, closed-door meeting of the Communist Party's Central Committee in Beijing. Sixteen of those expelled were from the military, according to the BBC, as party discipline and political loyalty took centre stage at the gathering.
Xi urged the Communist Party and the military to “turn the blade inward”, launch a self-revolution and root out “viruses” undermining their institutional health.
The fifth plenum of the current Central Committee was marked by an unprecedented number of absences in the post-Mao era. Only 279 members attended, compared with 315 at the previous plenum in October 2025 and 364 in July 2024. The committee, which began its term in 2022 with more than 370 members, has been steadily depleted by Xi's crackdown.
The party cited "serious disciplinary and legal violations" in its announcements, without providing details of the specific allegations against the officials.
Xi, who came to power in 2012, has made combating corruption a defining feature of his leadership. However, analysts say the campaign has increasingly become a means of enforcing political obedience and consolidating his authority, with even officials handpicked for senior positions failing to escape scrutiny.
Military purge leaves top ranks depleted
Among those expelled were former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui, former senior generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli, and prominent diplomat Liu Jianchao. Zhang Youxia was a vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC), the body responsible for overseeing China's armed forces, while Ma and Zhang were former members of the powerful Politburo.
The latest action follows the removal of former general He Weidong and other senior military figures in an earlier round of expulsions. The continuing purge has raised questions about the leadership and operational readiness of the People's Liberation Army (PLA), even as China showcases advances in its military capabilities.
The CMC has been reduced to just two members: Xi, its chairman, and Zhang Shengmin, its vice-chairman. The party elevated Zhang to the 24-member Politburo during the plenum, making him the only military representative on the top governing body.
The party also adopted a resolution calling for stricter internal discipline, stronger anti-corruption enforcement and greater ideological purity. According to state news agency Xinhua, the leadership said it must strengthen its long-term governing capacity and maintain close ties with the people.
The BBC reported that China's top anti-corruption watchdog had disciplined 680,000 people across the party apparatus in the first nine months of this year. The latest expulsions bring the number of members removed during Xi's third term to 51, compared with 35 in his first term and five in his second.
Amidst the purge, Zhang Shengmin, vice chair of the Central Military Commission, was promoted to the ruling Communist Party’s Politburo.
The 68-year-old veteran military official rose to become China’s second-highest-ranking general last year, during the fourth plenum.
Xi tightens grip ahead of 2027 leadership reshuffle
The timing of the crackdown is significant, with the next Communist Party Congress scheduled for the second half of 2027. The gathering will determine the party's next leadership line-up, and Xi is widely expected to seek a fourth term, extending his rule beyond the decade-long limit followed by his predecessors.
The scale of the purge suggests that the leadership is scrutinising officials more closely ahead of the reshuffle. Xi has repeatedly warned against cadres who profess loyalty but fail to follow party directives, reinforcing the view that political allegiance is central to the campaign.
Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China, told the BBC that the anti-corruption drive had increasingly become an effort to consolidate and maintain authority, rather than simply address graft.
The crackdown has also extended beyond the party and military. Reports cited by The Economist have highlighted the detention or disappearance of business executives and figures linked to strategically important industries, raising concerns about the consequences for China's business climate.

title: 'Educated voters don't turn up in assembly polls': UP minister OP Rajbhar plays down MLC results
raw_text:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar shrugged off the legislative council election results after the Samajwadi Party defeated the Bharatiya Janata Party in the Varanasi Graduates' constituency, saying the election reflected the mandate of educated voters rather than the general electorate.Speaking to reporters, Rajbhar said the MLC elections had no connection with the assembly elections.“This is the people’s mandate, the mandate of educated voters, and we welcome the verdict,” Rajbhar said.“However, these elections have no connection with the assembly elections. Historically, educated voters often do not turn up to vote in assembly elections and instead treat the day as a holiday,” he added.
The BJP won six seats and the Samajwadi Party won five of the 11 seats in the biennial elections. The results come months ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, widely seen as a test of popularity between the BJP and the SP.Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav described the BJP's performance in the MLC elections as a "double defeat" and said the results had laid the groundwork for his party's victory in the assembly polls.In a post on X, Akhilesh said the BJP lost the Varanasi Graduates' constituency in both the initial count and the recount, calling it a "double defeat of the double engine government".The SP chief said the BJP's defeat "was the defeat of its policies concerning teachers, students and education" and that "the educated unemployed graduates had also delivered their verdict" against the party.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

title: ‘Canada cannot be an EU member because of geography’: Von der Leyen proposes associate membership for Ottawa
raw_text:
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has proposed a new partnership between the European Union and Canada. The proposal involves an associate membership status that would bring Ottawa closer to the bloc without granting it full membership.
According to Reuters, von der Leyen said the EU was discussing the possibility of Canada becoming the bloc’s first associate member from outside Europe. She described the proposed arrangement as “association without accession”, saying it would bring the two sides closer than any partnership the EU had established before.
“Canada cannot be an EU member because of geography, but we want to take our relationship to the highest possible level,” von der Leyen said.
She added that associate membership would be reserved for the EU’s closest partners outside Europe, with the arrangement aimed at aligning policies more closely while stopping short of full membership.
The development comes as Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to diversify the country's trade ties and reduce its dependence on the United States amid escalating trade tensions with President Donald Trump.
Ottawa has been looking to strengthen economic and strategic ties with Europe, particularly in areas such as critical minerals, artificial intelligence, energy and defence, while opening up new markets for Canadian businesses.
Von der Leyen said the EU and Canada would seek to establish a “single space for strategic supply chains”, with both sides pursuing joint or complementary investments, including private financing.
The proposed cooperation aims to strengthen economic links and secure access to strategically important materials as both sides seek to reduce supply chain vulnerabilities.
She also said the two sides would work together to develop rules and standards for artificial intelligence, an area where closer regulatory coordination could strengthen their influence over global technology governance.
Von der Leyen further announced that the EU and Canada would finalise an agreement the following day to bring Canada into Europe's supercomputing infrastructure. Such cooperation could support scientific research, advanced computing and AI development by improving collaboration between European and Canadian researchers.
On security, von der Leyen said the two sides needed to adjust their strategic posture in the Arctic to defend their shared values.
The region has gained geopolitical importance because of its natural resources, emerging maritime routes and strategic position, increasing the need for closer coordination among Western partners

title: A customer booked a Mahindra XUV700 in 2022 but never received the SUV; four years later, a consumer commission has ordered Mahindra and its dealer to refund the booking amount with interest and pay Rs 62,000
raw_text:
NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Haryana has held Mahindra & Mahindra and its authorised dealer guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice after they failed to deliver a booked SUV or refund the advance payment. The commission directed them to refund Rs 21,000 with interest, pay Rs 51,000 as compensation and Rs 11,000 in litigation expenses.
In its October 7, 2026, order, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Yamuna Nagar, at Jagadhri, held the dealer and manufacturer jointly and severally liable, directing them to comply within 45 days.
Booked Mahindra XUV700 never delivered
According to the commission order, the customer booked a Mahindra XUV700 diesel automatic in Everest White on February 8, 2022, and paid Rs 21,000 as advance booking money. He was assured that the vehicle would be delivered within six to eight months.
When he contacted the dealer in October 2022, after waiting nine months, he was told to wait another month. In November, he was again assured that delivery would happen soon.
But in December 2022, the customer checked the vehicle’s booking status online and was surprised to find it marked as invoiced or sold. He alleged that the vehicle booked for him had been sold to someone else. 
When he questioned the dealer, he was not given a satisfactory answer and was asked to wait longer.
The customer also lodged a complaint with the manufacturer through its toll-free number. He said the grievance was registered, but the issue remained unresolved. The SUV was never delivered, and the booking amount was not returned, prompting him to approach the commission in February 2025.
However, the dealer denied promising delivery within six to eight months, claiming its staff had tried to contact the customer several times but received no response, so the SUV was allotted to the next person in line. It also denied receiving any extra money. Mahindra & Mahindra said the dealer was a separate entity responsible for the sale and claimed the customer had cancelled the booking, making him ineligible for relief.
Commission’s finding
The bench comprising president 
Rajbir Singh and members 
Jasvinder Singh and 
Suman Rana found that the dealer and manufacturer gave contradictory explanations about who received the booking amount and why the SUV was not delivered.
The commission observed that “the opponents are self contradictory” in their claims about the payment and the customer’s alleged cancellation of the booking.
It noted that neither side produced evidence to show that the customer had been contacted about delivery or had cancelled the booking. The commission also found no proof that the booking amount had been refunded or that the customer was informed the SUV had been allotted to someone else.
The bench said the dealer and manufacturer could not escape liability by blaming each other.
It observed that “it is the prime duty of opponents to ensure the delivery of the booked vehicle within time to the consumer/customer”. Holding both guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, the commission said their failure to deliver the SUV, refund the booking amount or resolve the grievance had caused the customer mental agony and harassment.
Final order
The commission allowed the complaint and directed the dealer and manufacturer, jointly and severally, to:
- Refund the Rs 21,000 booking amount with 9 percent annual interest from the date the complaint was filed until payment.
- Pay Rs 51,000 as compensation for the harassment and inconvenience caused.
- Pay Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.
The order said the parties must comply within 45 days. If they fail to do so, the amounts awarded under the compensation and litigation-expense heads will carry 12 percent annual interest from the date of filing the complaint until realisation.

title: Israel election results: Netanyahu's bloc wins 53 seats, falls short of majority as coalition talks loom
raw_text:
The counting of votes in Israel’s election has confirmed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud as the largest party in the next Knesset, but left his right-wing bloc short of a parliamentary majority.
According to official figures released by Israel’s Central Elections Committee (CEC), cited by Jerusalem Post, Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats, while the opposition bloc seeking to replace him won 48. The results leave both sides well short of the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset, with Arab parties emerging as crucial players after winning a combined 19 seats.
The final tally, which included the remaining double-envelope ballots, confirmed Likud’s position as the largest party with 27 seats. United Torah Judaism and Otzma Yehudit won seven seats each, while Shas and the Religious Zionist Party secured six apiece. The results differed from several pre-election television polls, which had projected fewer seats for Likud and stronger performances by some of its allies.
With neither camp able to command a majority on its own, attention will now turn to coalition-building efforts and the possibility of a minority or unity government.
Israeli President Isaac Herzog is expected to consult party representatives after the formal publication of the final results before nominating a candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government. If the candidate fails, another leader could be given an opportunity. Failure to complete the process within the stipulated timeframe could eventually trigger another election.
A unity government involving Likud and opposition parties such as Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar, Naftali Bennett’s Together faction and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu could command 66 seats. However, such an arrangement appears unlikely at present, given the opposition’s campaign pledge to remove Netanyahu from power and his dependence on far-right and ultra-Orthodox allies.
The Arab parties’ combined tally could also prove decisive if Eisenkot’s bloc attempts to form a minority government with their support from outside the coalition.
The final count comes amid allegations of election interference and voter fraud. CEC chairman Noam Sohlberg asked Shin Bet chief David Zini to investigate suspicions that foreign entities may have attempted to influence voting in the Arab sector. However, the committee said there was no basis for claims of systematic damage to the election’s integrity.

title: SIR deadlines extended in 5 states, Delhi; EC sets new dates for final rolls
raw_text:
NEW DELHI: The Election Commission of India has revised the schedule for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Delhi, extending the deadline for final publication of voter lists.According to separate letters issued by the commission on October 29, the final electoral rolls for Haryana, Telangana, Nagaland, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra will be published on November 30. For Delhi, the final publication has been pushed to December 22.
The notice and claims-and-objections phase has also been extended, with revised deadlines varying by state. In Delhi, the period for filing claims and objections runs until November 25, while the notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will continue until December 15.In Maharashtra, the claims-and-objections phase will run until November 25, while the period for filing claims and objections ends on November 13. In Nagaland, the notice phase and disposal of claims and objections will continue until November 25. Haryana’s corresponding phase has been extended until November 20, while Telangana’s will continue until November 26.The commission has directed the officials concerned to publicise the revised schedules and inform political parties in writing.

title: Jamia sets date for student union poll, revokes disciplinary action against protesters
raw_text:
The university has also decided to hold students’ union elections within six weeks of the commencement of the next academic session
NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia has set May 15, 2027, as the deadline for approving and implementing its students’ union constitution and decided to revoke disciplinary action against protesting students. The university has also decided to hold students’ union elections within six weeks of the commencement of the next academic session, addressing three key demands raised by students during their 18-day protest seeking the restoration of the elected union, which has remained defunct since 2006.A student said the university had accepted all three demands, including a fixed deadline for implementing the constitution, an election schedule and the withdrawal of disciplinary proceedings against protesters.“Order has come in, it covers 3 points: 1) The approval and implementation of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union Constitution shall be completed by 15th May, 2027. We had demanded a date and they have announced a date, 2) The elections shall be conducted within 6 weeks of the start of the academic session, that is approximately within 6 weeks from 16 July 2027, 3) All disciplinary actions (taken against protesting students) will be revoked.
They have accepted all 3 of our demands...We are calling off our hunger strike and protest...”The decision comes amid mounting tensions on campus over the demand for the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union (JMISU). Students had continued their agitation despite an earlier university order stating that elections would be held within 15 days of the approval of the union’s constitution. They had questioned the absence of a deadline for approving the constitution.
The administration had also initiated disciplinary proceedings against students during the agitation. On October 27, the provost of Begum Hazrat Mahal Girls’ Hostel issued a show-cause notice to a student for allegedly obtaining emergency leave on misleading grounds and participating in the protest. The student was asked to submit a written explanation within 24 hours.The university has extended online classes until November 24 and shifted odd-semester examinations to online mode, citing the prevailing campus situation and concerns over students’ safety and security.
