title: India ready to share its battle-tested expertise with Asean partners to boost joint capabilities: Rajnath
raw_text:
NEW DELHI: India’s extensive expertise in counter-terrorism is not theoretical classroom knowledge but it is an experience hard-earned on the ground through decades of directly confronting complex, cross-border security challenges, defence minister 
Rajnath Singh
 said in the Philippines on Thursday.
Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) - Plus in Cebu, Rajnath underlined that “every strategy of India has been tested, refined and proven in the crucible of real-world operations” and that India stands fully prepared to share its practical, battle-tested experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes, and robust intelligence sharing to strengthen collective capabilities. He reaffirmed the country’s commitment to collective regional security and eradication of terrorism in all its forms.
Rajnath said this proactive, battle-tested doctrine was decisively demonstrated during Operation Sindoor, when India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a non-negotiable red line against state-sponsored terror. He stressed that counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, and India and Malaysia are co-chairing the experts’ working group on counter-terrorism for the 2024 to 2027 cycle.
Rajnath highlighted that by deploying frontline warships, India has successfully escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of high-seas hijackings, extending protection to commercial shipping irrespective of flag or nationality. He termed the security of commercial shipping as India’s responsibility. “In an era where global trade routes face complex transnational threats, India stands ready to move beyond rhetoric. There is a need for effective action, regular operational presence and international cooperation. India will continue serving as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific,” he said.
The minister highlighted the importance of youth engagement in strengthening India-ASEAN defence cooperation, stating that the shared demographic profile and aspirations of the young populations provide a strong foundation for deeper regional partnership. He proposed the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to enhance institutional people-to-people connectivity, promote digital innovation and facilitate capacity building in line with ADMM-Plus initiatives.
Rajnath Singh with Australian and Japanese defence ministers
On the sidelines of ADMM-Plus, Rajnath met Japanese minister of defence Shinjiro Koizumi, and Australian minister for defence Richard Marles and posted a picture with them. “JAI: Japan, Australia, India”, the defence Minister posted on X, with him holding hands of both Marles and Koizumi, as he stood in the middle.
At the forum, the minister reiterated that India attaches importance to ASEAN centrality and a secure, open, inclusive, resilient and rule-based Indo-Pacific, where peace and stability are not just aspirations but a result of collective commitment. He stated that its strategic engagement with ASEAN is long-term and rooted in shared interests, mutual respect and practical cooperation. He recalled that the second ASEAN-India defence ministers’ informal meeting in Kuala Lumpur in Oct last year reaffirmed the commitment to advancing the defence and security components of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the ASEAN-India Plan of Action for 2026 to 2030.
On the theme of 13th ADMM-Plus ‘Navigating Our Future, Together’, Rajnath stated it resonates with India’s foreign and defence policy paradigms as well as its civilisational ethos of ‘Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah’ (May all beings be happy) that reflects the aspiration for the happiness, prosperity, and well-being of all the people across the world. “This theme reminds us that our greatest strength lies in our solidarity and the shared ability to leverage our geographic, economic and strategic diversity. India believes in an international system built on mutual trust, co-operation, and collective responsibility. It is this precise collaborative spirit that empowers us to overcome the challenges to peace and order,” he said.
The minister described maritime cooperation as crucial to India’s engagement with ASEAN during 2026, highlighting New Delhi’s designation of 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and the conduct of the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He emphasised that India does not merely preach the tenets of international maritime law; it is a steadfast practitioner of global laws concerning maritime security. “Our commitment to ensuring the freedom of navigation and safeguarding global Sea Lines of Communication is backed by a continuous, decades-long operational legacy. Since 2008, the Indian Navy has maintained an uninterrupted, active presence in highly volatile corridors like the Gulf of Aden, without coercion or unilateral actions that undermine the rights of other nations,” he said.
Rajnath said India’s emphasis on the rule of law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and its advocacy for freedom of navigation and overflight are not directed against any country but are meant to safeguard the collective interests of all regional stakeholders who depend on open sea lanes and stable maritime governance.

title: 'Transgressions by China happen, it's not new': Arunachal CM says no intrusion along LAC
raw_text:
Arunachal Pradesh CM Pema Khandu asserted that the situation along the LAC remained normal.
NEW DELHI: Arunachal Pradesh chief minister Pema Khandu on Thursday said transgressions along the India-China border were not new, asserting that the situation in the state’s border areas remained normal and that Indian armed forces were guarding the frontier effectively."Transgression has happened, no doubt. But it keeps happening; it is not a new thing," news agency PTI reported him as saying. Khandu added that the border was not clearly demarcated.Responding to questions about recent remarks on confrontations between Indian and Chinese troops at several locations along the Arunachal Pradesh border, Khandu said China did not recognise the McMahon Line, which separates Arunachal Pradesh from Tibet.
"Arunachal shares a very long border with Tibet-China, nearly 1,200 km. So, patrolling parties from their side sometimes cross over to our side. It's a transgression, not an intrusion," he said, without specifying the incidents he was referring to.Last week, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Director General Shatrujeet Kapur had said confrontations with Chinese troops continued at several locations along the border in Arunachal Pradesh, triggering a controversy.
Khandu said he had come across the issue in news reports and described the matter as one that was being widely discussed."The media has unnecessarily ratcheted it up. The situation right now is normal, and our armed forces are guarding the border very well. There is no matter of tension right now," he said.
Khandu was speaking ahead of the inauguration of the 14th International Tourism Mart in Tawang, attended by Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat and other dignitaries.Shekhawat said India’s borders were secure under the Narendra Modi government and there was no cause for concern. He also alleged that attempts were being made to create a false narrative around the issue.In August 2005, the Ministry of External Affairs had informed the Rajya Sabha that China disputed the legality of the McMahon Line dividing Arunachal Pradesh and the Tibet Autonomous Region.The ministry had also said that India and China had differing perceptions of the Line of Actual Control (LAC), with both sides conducting patrols in border areas and instances of transgression by Chinese military personnel occurring from time to time.

title: Days after the US Department of Energy announced Power Grid Emergency in 13 States; government declares national emergency to secure bulk power system: What it is, and what it means for Americans
raw_text:
US government has announced a national emergency to protect the country’s electricity grid from potential security risks posed by foreign-made equipment. In an executive order signed by President Trump, the government authorised restrictions on certain foreign-made equipment that could pose risks to national security, including equipment used in power generation, transmission and grid operations. The order also allows officials to impose security conditions on existing installations and replace equipment deemed risky. The move comes days after the US Department of Energy issued an emergency order in 13 States on October 12 authorising PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission operator serving much of the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions, to run designated power generation units as needed to protect grid stability.
What the national emergency means in this case
The national emergency declaration allows the US government to take stricter measures against foreign-made equipment that could pose security risks to the country's electricity grid. Under the order, the Energy Department can restrict the purchase, import and installation of certain equipment if officials determine that it could expose critical infrastructure to cyberattacks, unauthorised access or supply disruptions.
Notably, the order does not ban all foreign-made electrical equipment. Instead, it targets equipment linked to designated foreign entities that the government considers a security risk. It also allows officials to impose security requirements on existing installations, including monitoring, isolation or replacement of equipment deemed unsafe.
Why is US doing this now
The order says the risks have become more serious as the US becomes increasingly dependent on reliable electricity to support AI data centres, advanced manufacturing, defence production and other critical infrastructure.
“The rapid growth of advanced manufacturing, data centers, artificial intelligence, and defense production has increased the Nation’s dependence on abundant, reliable electricity and magnified the consequences of a successful attack or supply disruption on the bulk-power system,” the order says.
A disruption to the electricity grid could affect businesses, essential services and national security. The administration argues that reducing reliance on potentially vulnerable foreign suppliers would help protect the network.
It further stated that the “continued United States reliance on foreign sources of bulk-power system electric equipment with these potential national security vulnerabilities also creates a supply chain vulnerability that could eliminate the supply of these products in the United States as a result of disruptions in international trade or other causes.”
What it means for Americans
For Americans, the national emergency order could lead to tighter security checks on equipment used to supply electricity to homes, businesses and critical infrastructure. The government may require utilities to monitor, secure or replace certain equipment identified as a potential security risk. However, the order does not mean consumers will immediately face changes to their electricity supply.
The move could also create opportunities for US manufacturers of transformers, generators and other power grid equipment as the government seeks to prioritise domestically made products. However, replacing existing equipment and shifting supply chains could involve additional costs for utilities and manufacturers.

title: Jammu & Kashmir HC strikes down water tax on hydropower projects
raw_text:
SRINAGAR: In a setback to J&K govt, the high court (HC) of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh Thursday struck down the 2010 Water Resources Act, ruling that water usage charges levied on hydropower projects amounted to a tax on electricity generation, a subject beyond the erstwhile state legislature’s powers.A division bench of Justices Sanjay Dhar and Rajnesh Oswal quashed demand notices issued to 13 independent power producers and restrained J&K govt from imposing any tax on electricity generation under the guise of water usage charges or any other levy.
The producers had challenged the law, arguing that charges fixed by Water Resources Regulatory Authority on April 2, 2019, were linked to the height from which water drove turbines rather than the volume consumed, effectively taxing power generation.Govt defended the levy, citing its authority to regulate water storage and use, National Water Policy and the need to conserve J&K’s water resources.Rejecting its arguments, HC held that the legislation exceeded the erstwhile state’s legislative competence when enacted. It also dismissed J&K govt’s contention that the law’s subsequent adoption under Jammu & Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, had legitimised it.HC observed that a law unconstitutional at the time of enactment could not be validated merely through its subsequent adoption by Parliament.

“E-Revive Pune: Driving Change Through Responsible E-Waste Disposal” is a CSR initiative focused on promoting responsible e-waste management through awareness, organised collection, and certified recycling systems within the city.
Pune is widely known as one of India’s prominent centres for education, technology, and industry. With a large student population, expanding residential neighbourhoods, growing corporate workplaces, and active commercial markets, the city represents a dynamic urban ecosystem where the use of electronic devices is deeply integrated into everyday life. From educational institutions and professional workplaces to households and retail markets, technology plays a central role in how the city functions. As a result, managing electronic waste responsibly has become an important aspect of sustainable urban living.
Through E-Revive Pune, the initiative engages key communities across the city, including schools and colleges, residential housing societies, corporate offices, and marketplaces, helping people understand the nature of e-waste, the importance of safe handling, and the need for responsible recycling.
The campaign begins with structured awareness sessions that encourage informed disposal practices and responsible technology use. These engagements are followed by organised e-waste collection drives, enabling participants to safely dispose of unused or end-of-life electronic devices.
All collected e-waste is transferred through authorised channels to certified recycling facilities, where it is processed in accordance with established environmental standards.
By combining awareness, accessible collection mechanisms, and responsible recycling processes, E-Revive Pune aims to support more sustainable e-waste management practices across the city.
Smaller electrical devices used at home: Toasters, Vacuum Cleaners, Coffee Machine, Hair dryer.
Devices used for computing and data processing: Computers, Laptops, printers, Routers, Keyboards.
Gadgets and devices used for entertainment and communication: Television, Smartphones, Tablets, audio systems.
Electrically powered toys and entertainment devices: Electronic toys, Remote controlled cars, video game consoles.
Lighting devices & fixtures: LED Bulbs, fluorescent tubes, Desk lamps, chandeliers.
Machines that automatically dispense products or services: Vending machines, ticket dispensers, hand sanitizer dispensers.
Devices for monitoring and controlling various systems: Smoke detectors, thermostats, security systems, pressure gauges.
E-waste’ means electrical and electronic equipment, whole or in part discarded as waste by the consumer or bulk consumer as well as rejects from manufacturing, refurbishment and repair processes.
Our goal is to educate and mobilize different sectors of society viz Residential Welfare Associations (RWA), offices, retail markets, and educational institutions on E-waste.
E-waste is growing in India at the rate of 10%. Major recycling of E-waste is conducted in the non-formal sector using primitive and hazardous methods. Our aim is to educate, manage and collect E-waste efficiently to help India better manage the problem.
The city that is in focus is Pune. Within the city, we would be reaching out to Residential Welfare Associations (RWA), offices, retail markets, and educational institutions.
You can call the Teach India E-waste National Solutions Centre on +91-7208640496 to be a part of the program/ join through by filling in the details through the form as provided in the Join Us section of the website. SACH & Teach India aims to increase awareness regarding the significance of e-waste disposal and educate callers on proper e-waste handling practices. Additionally, the E-waste gathered will be collected in Mobile Vans by Teach India from each cohort. These vans will deposit the E-waste collected in centralized collection facilities.
The initiative focuses on: 1. Educating the public at large through awareness sessions/ digital and print mediums about E-waste, its proper management and disposal, and the significance of E-waste management. 2. Collection and responsible disposal of the e-waste at the authorized recycling centers.
Over the total duration of the project, we aim to collect at least 90 metric tonnes of E-waste from the city we plan to conduct the drive.
After E-waste is collected, it's first segregated by material type. Devices that can be repaired are refurbished for reuse. Non-reusable items are disassembled to recover valuable materials, while hazardous components are treated separately. Finally, remaining parts are shredded and recycled, minimizing environmental impact.

title: Built in 1925 and vacant for over 20 years, Texas’s historic Imperial Sugar Char House survived stalled redevelopment plans; the city has approved a $15 million rescue, with preservation work due through 2028
raw_text:
After more than two decades of vacancy, failed redevelopment plans and gradual deterioration, Sugar Land’s historic Imperial Sugar Char House is finally set to receive the rescue many residents have waited years to see. The Sugar Land City Council approved a $15 million preservation project on October 20, according to Chron, with work expected to begin later this year and finish in 2028.
The Char House, built in 1925, is one of the most recognisable remnants of the Imperial Sugar refinery that helped shape the identity of Sugar Land, Texas. The building has stood empty since the refinery closed in 2003, and repeated efforts to bring the surrounding Imperial Historic District back to life never made it past the planning stage. Now the city has taken direct control of the landmark’s future and committed real money to keeping it standing.
A building tied to Sugar Land’s story
The Char House was constructed during the height of Imperial Sugar’s influence, when the refinery was not only a major employer but also the reason the community became known as Sugar Land. The building formed part of a larger industrial campus that processed and stored sugar, and its distinctive presence has long made it a symbol of the city’s origins.
When the refinery portion of the campus closed in 2003, the Char House entered a long period of uncertainty. The property remained vacant for more than 20 years, and the city says the building began to deteriorate during that time. Local police also reported issues with trespassing, despite warnings, patrols and arrests around the site.
For preservation supporters, the concern was never simply about saving an old industrial structure. The Char House represents a physical link to the workers, families and businesses that built Sugar Land around the sugar industry. Mayor Carol K. McCutcheon described it as more than an iconic building, calling it a connection to the community’s history and origins, as per the report.
Why earlier plans failed
The site’s troubles were not caused by a lack of interest. Developers repeatedly proposed ways to redevelop the Imperial Historic District, but financing and market conditions repeatedly got in the way. The most ambitious plan arrived in 2023, when PUMA Development announced a $1 billion mixed-use redevelopment for the 20-acre district, it was reported.
That proposal promised a dramatic transformation, with residential units, retail space, offices and restaurants planned across the historic site. It appeared to offer the kind of large-scale investment that could have revived the Char House and the land around it. But the developer ultimately abandoned the project after failing to secure financing, leaving the historic building in the same vulnerable condition it had occupied for years.
The pattern illustrates a familiar challenge in historic preservation. Old industrial buildings can be expensive to repair, difficult to adapt and complicated to insure. Developers may see their potential, but banks and investors can hesitate when the cost of stabilising a century-old structure competes with newer construction elsewhere.
In Sugar Land’s case, the city eventually decided that waiting for another private redevelopment plan carried too much risk. Officials acquired the larger Imperial Historic District in June 2025, giving the municipality control over the property and allowing it to begin addressing the building’s condition directly.
What the $15 million project includes
The approved project is not a full commercial redevelopment, at least not yet. Instead, it focuses on stabilising and protecting the Char House so that it can survive long enough for a future use to be developed. The city says the work will prepare the building for eventual redevelopment and adaptive reuse.
The preservation plan includes a new permanent roof, structural repairs to the exterior walls and rear liquor gallery, selective steel and masonry repairs, mechanical and electrical improvements, and restoration of the building’s windows. The city’s iconic Imperial signage will also be restored and returned to its historic location on the building.
Those repairs matter because water intrusion, weakened walls and failing mechanical systems can quickly turn a vacant historic building into a safety hazard. A new roof and structural work can prevent further decay, while restored windows and improved electrical systems make future occupation more realistic. The city also says the work is designed to keep the building eligible for future historic tax credits, which could make redevelopment more financially viable later.
A groundbreaking is expected on November 5, with construction mobilisation planned for December. The city estimates that the preservation work will be completed by March 2028.
What could happen next
The city has not yet announced a final tenant or a complete redevelopment plan for the restored building. However, officials say the Char House could eventually accommodate office, commercial, retail or restaurant uses as broader plans for the Imperial Historic District move forward.
That flexibility is important. A restored industrial building can serve many purposes, from a restaurant or event space to offices or small commercial units. The key is that the city is first protecting the structure rather than allowing it to deteriorate further while developers wait for the right economic conditions.
For residents, the project represents a shift from uncertainty to action. After years of watching proposals appear and disappear, they will soon see crews on site, scaffolding around the building and visible progress toward saving a landmark that has defined Sugar Land for a century.
A second chance for a landmark
The Char House has survived longer than many expected. It outlasted the closure of the refinery, more than 20 years of vacancy and the collapse of a billion-dollar redevelopment proposal. Now, with $15 million approved and construction scheduled through 2028, it may finally receive the care needed to become part of Sugar Land’s future as well as its past.
The project will not solve every question about the wider Imperial Historic District, and the city will still need to determine how best to use the restored space. But for now, the focus is on preservation. Sugar Land is investing in the idea that some buildings are worth saving, not only because of what they once were, but because of what they can still become.

title: MLC poll setback opens new front within Mahayuti; Shinde-for-CM pitch, 'Shakuni mama' jibe fly
raw_text:
NEW DELHI: Cracks within Maharashtra's ruling Mahayuti alliance came out in the open on Thursday after a Shiv Sena leader advocated for deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde to be elevated to the post of chief minister.Speaking to reporters after the MLC election results, former MLA Ravindra Dhangekar said the outcome reflected people's views of the Devendra Fadnavis-led government."When there are doubts about the state government's image, such results are a reflection of it," Dhangekar said."When Eknath Shinde was chief minister, he helped Mahayuti come to power. Shinde should again become chief minister," he added.Dhangekar's remarks were quickly rebuked by the BJP, which said the Shiv Sena leader had no authority to comment on the issue."Out of 149 contested seats (in the 2024 assembly elections), BJP won 137," senior BJP minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule said.MLC Pravin Darekar also lashed out at Dhangekar and advised him to "stay within his limits".
"The state is progressing like never before under Fadnavis's leadership. He hates Fadnavis so much that he never misses an opportunity to criticise him," the BJP leader said."We never made any comment against your leadership and will never do so.
We will not tolerate your attempts to tarnish Fadnavis's image," Darekar added.The remarks came after the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi won three of the five graduates' and teachers' constituencies of the legislative council that went to the polls on October 23. Meanwhile, Mahayuti bagged two seats.
Meanwhile, BJP leader and Maharashtra minister Nitesh Rane called for identifying "Shakuni mamas" within the ruling Mahayuti alliance after its lacklustre performance in the MLC elections."It is time to find out whether there are any 'Shakuni mamas' within Mahayuti who follow the scripts that Uddhav Thackeray likes," he said.Shakuni is a character in the Mahabharata known for creating discord and plotting against others.Rane said the ruling alliance had not achieved the expected success, but the BJP had still won two seats in constituencies it had not contested in the previous election."We fought as one force in the assembly elections, taking up the Hindutva agenda, and the results were evident. Our allies must understand the strength of Mahayuti," he said."Our candidate was ahead by 4,500 votes in the first-preference count. The Congress candidate won because of Nitesh Karale's second-preference votes. The Congress should thank Karale," he said.
Rohitashwa Ranjan is a digital journalist with The Times of India, where he decodes Indian politics as a carefully staged production with scripts, subtext and everything behind. His stories track elections, party dynamics and the things that often are buried beneath the headlines. When not parsing vote shares or alliances, he is usually reading between the lines, where the real story tends to reside.

title: Map that came to symbolise America's divide over slavery auctioned for nearly $1 million
raw_text:
A hand-drawn map of the Mason-Dixon Line, which became a symbol of the divide between free and slave states in the United States, sold for $950,000 at an auction in Asheville, North Carolina, on Thursday. Forty-five bidders competed for the historic document, with the contest lasting just under three minutes.
The bidding began at $400,000 for the survey, completed in 1768 by British surveyors Charles Mason and Jeremiah Dixon. The sale was conducted both online and in person at Brunk Auctions. Although the final price fell short of the auction house's high estimate of $1.2 million, its vice-president Lauren Brunk said she was pleased with the result.
“It’s a very high price for a map," she said.
The buyer has asked to remain anonymous, at least for now, Brunk said. The Library of Congress, which lost out when the map was sold in 1982, did not participate in Thursday's bidding.
The map was originally commissioned to resolve a boundary dispute between the colonies of Maryland and Pennsylvania. However, its historical significance grew over time as the Mason-Dixon Line became associated with the division between the northern free states and the southern slave states.
The line was later used in the 1820 Missouri Compromise to establish limits on slavery in the young United States. It became synonymous with the deep divisions over slavery that ultimately led to the American Civil War four decades later.
The late publisher Malcolm Forbes bought the map in 1982 for $360,000, outbidding the Library of Congress. It was sold again in 2002 for $556,000, making Thursday's sale a significant increase over its previous auction price.
Brunk said she was pleased that the historic document had been entrusted to the auction house.
“I would like to say I’m thrilled that this is going to a good home and we are so happy to have had it in our presence for these last months,” Brunk said. “It also feels like a privilege to have been entrusted to steward this one owner to the next.”
A vertical section of the map depicting the Delaware-Maryland border is housed at Princeton University.

title: George Michael’s ‘Faith’ guitar sells for £234,000; Siobhan Bailey’s brother Gerard objects to auction by estranged husband Ian Belcher, claiming she wanted the memorabilia left to her nieces and nephews
raw_text:
George Michael
’s iconic guitar from his 1987 hit 'Faith' music video has sold for £234,000 at auction, amid a family dispute over the sale of the late singer’s personal memorabilia. The instrument was among 32 lots from the collection of Siobhan Bailey, Michael’s longtime personal assistant and trusted confidante, being auctioned by Sworders.
According to the BBC, the auction sparked a dispute between Bailey’s family and her estranged husband, Ian Belcher, who is selling the items after inheriting them following her death in 2014. Her brother, Gerard Bailey, has strongly objected to the sale, claiming his sister would have been horrified to see her cherished possessions auctioned off.
Why George Michael’s guitar auction sparked a family dispute
The guitar, which Michael played in the video for 'Faith', was gifted to Siobhan Bailey by the singer, according to her brother. Bailey worked with Michael for two decades, beginning in 1984, when his band Wham! was enjoying its rise to fame.
Gerard told the BBC that his sister was in the process of divorcing Belcher when she died suddenly at the age of 56. However, the couple were still legally married, and she had not left a registered will. As a result, her estate passed to Belcher.
Her brother claimed that Siobhan had begun preparing a will shortly before her death, intending to leave the items to her nieces and nephews, but the document was never registered. 
He also argued that, had she lived a few weeks longer, the possessions would not have passed to her estranged husband.
There is no suggestion that Belcher lacks the legal right to sell the items. However, Gerard has criticised the decision to conduct the auction under his sister’s name and has asked that the sale be cancelled or promoted in Belcher’s name instead.
In a letter to the auction house, seen by the BBC, Gerard described the auction as a breach of his sister’s privacy. He also called the use of her name “disingenuous” and “wholly unethical”, while describing the decision to profit from the collection as “egregiously shameful”.
He told the BBC that his sister “would be horrified at the prospect of the auction being held in her name and that her personal, cherished possessions are being sold off to the highest bidder”.
Both Sworders and Belcher declined to comment on the dispute.
George Michael’s guitar played a key role in his solo reinvention
Siobhan Bailey’s brother Gerard has objected to the auction of memorabilia belonging to the late George Michael aide. (Photo: Instagram)
The Gretsch Synchromatic guitar featured prominently in the 1987 music video for 'Faith', one of Michael’s most recognisable solo hits. In the video, the singer appeared in ripped blue Levi’s jeans, a white T-shirt and a black leather biker jacket, strumming the acoustic instrument.
Michael had reportedly bought the guitar from a shop in Los Angeles shortly before filming the video. Its appearance became closely associated with his transformation from a teen pop idol in Wham! into a successful solo artist.
Guitarist magazine recently described it as “arguably the most famous Gretsch Synchromatic in the world”.
The instrument was initially estimated to fetch between £60,000 and £120,000, but ultimately sold for £234,000, significantly exceeding the upper end of its estimate.
Other George Michael memorabilia also went under the hammer
The auction featured 32 items from Bailey’s collection, including personal documents, photographs and memorabilia associated with Michael and Wham! Several items reportedly attracted bids above their estimates.
Among them was a Filofax from Michael’s 1988 'Faith' tour, containing Bailey’s handwritten notes and annotations. It had an estimated value of up to £600, but received a bid of £1,750.
Other lots included a note from Michael and Wham! bandmate Andrew Ridgeley, signed photographs, an invitation to Ridgeley’s 21st birthday party, and gold and platinum awards presented to Bailey to mark sales milestones achieved by Michael’s music.
Gerard said his sister was proud of the personalised music awards but had remained modest about her association with the singer. He also maintained that she would never have agreed to the sale of her personal papers and correspondence.
“I think she’d be devastated that something as personal as her Filofax and notes from George are up for grabs. It’s just so tawdry and contrary to how she was,” he told the BBC.
He added that the family believed the possessions should have remained with them and accused Belcher of deciding, 12 years after his sister’s death, to “cash in” on the collection.
Siobhan Bailey’s two-decade association with George Michael
Bailey began working as Michael’s personal assistant in 1984, the year Wham! scored their first UK number-one hit with 'Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go'. She remained in the role for 20 years, helping the singer navigate the demands of fame while protecting his privacy.
According to her brother, she was among the few people Michael deeply trusted and whose opinions he valued.
“I think she was one of the few people George trusted and whose opinion he valued,” Gerard told the BBC. “She was always honest and straight with him. I guess that’s why she stayed working for him for so long through the very, very good and not so good times.”
He said the guitar was a gift from Michael because the singer thought so highly of his sister.
Michael, who rose to international fame with Wham! before building a hugely successful solo career with songs including 'Careless Whisper', 'Father Figure', 'Faith', 'Outside' and 'Fastlove', died in 2016.
Sworders auctioneer Guy Schooling told Guitarist magazine that Belcher had been traumatised by Bailey’s sudden death and had kept the memorabilia stored in his garage for years. Schooling said Belcher was eventually persuaded that the items could not remain there indefinitely because they risked deteriorating.
Bailey’s family, however, remains opposed to the sale, arguing that the collection represents a deeply personal chapter in her life and her relationship with one of pop music’s most celebrated artists.

title: Netanyahu's unity government gambit: Can he lure Eisenkot from opposition?
raw_text:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is exploring ways to form a national unity government with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot following the October 27 election. Meanwhile, Yisrael Beytenu chairman Avigdor Liberman also appears to be distancing himself from the opposition bloc and favouring a unity arrangement, according to reports published in The Jerusalem Post and Maariv.
According to the report, sources close to Netanyahu are reportedly promoting a plan to bring Eisenkot into a government led by the Likud chief, despite Eisenkot's pledge not to serve under him. Meanwhile, N12 News reported on Wednesday that Liberman had cut off contact with Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, and had stopped answering calls from his opposition counterparts.
The developments come as the Central Elections Committee continues to update the results. Its final report is not expected to be submitted to the president until next week. Netanyahu's ability to form a government will depend on the final seat count and whether he can secure support beyond his existing bloc.
Netanyahu camp explores power-sharing deal
Netanyahu declared in his speech at the Jerusalem International Convention Center that "We must establish a strong national right-wing government." However, sources close to him began briefing reporters that same night on a possible unity government involving Eisenkot.
According to the sources, Likud officials believe Eisenkot has few viable alternatives. They argue that the opposition bloc has exhausted its electoral potential, including among Israelis who travelled from abroad to vote. They also believe the high turnout in the Arab sector would be difficult to replicate in another election.
The officials say Israelis living abroad are unlikely to purchase expensive plane tickets to vote again just a few months later.
Sources close to Netanyahu claim that "Eisenkot will not survive another round and may even lose his position as head of the bloc."
They believe Eisenkot could eventually agree to join a Netanyahu-led government despite his previous commitments. However, the reports do not indicate that Eisenkot has agreed to consider the proposal.
Two possible arrangements under discussion
The briefings from Netanyahu's circle have outlined different versions of a possible agreement.
Under one proposal, Netanyahu would offer Eisenkot the second half of the prime ministerial term under a rotation arrangement. Likud officials say Netanyahu would remain in office until the end of US President Donald Trump's term, "finish the job in Iran", and lead regional peace initiatives before handing over the premiership to Eisenkot after about two years.
Under another version, Netanyahu would refuse to agree to a rotation and instead offer Eisenkot a senior ministerial portfolio.
The proposed framework would initially bring together Netanyahu, Eisenkot, National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, without the ultra-Orthodox parties.
According to Likud figures promoting the plan, the ultra-Orthodox parties want to resolve the military conscription issue. However, their rabbis fear that public and political responsibility for legislation allowing ultra-Orthodox men to be drafted into the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) would fall on them.
Under the proposal, the government would first pass the conscription law without the ultra-Orthodox parties participating in the coalition. Those parties could then join the government after the legislation is approved, expanding its support.
Netanyahu's associates believe the arrangement could give Eisenkot a significant achievement on military conscription and persuade him to join the government.
Opposition rejects prospect of Eisenkot joining Netanyahu
Eisenkot has previously pledged not to serve under Netanyahu, and political figures remain sceptical about the proposed arrangement.
Sources in the opposition bloc have categorically rejected the possibility of Eisenkot joining a Netanyahu-led government, describing such a move as "complete suicide, both morally and politically".
Some political figures, including those on the Right, argue that joining Netanyahu at this stage could end Eisenkot's political career. They also question whether pressure from President Isaac Herzog or Trump would change his position.
They point to the precedent of Benny Gantz agreeing to a rotation arrangement with Netanyahu only after three rounds of elections, amid the coronavirus crisis and growing public frustration over political deadlock.
The political climate has since changed, these figures argue. Opposition voters are reportedly more willing to lift the boycott of Arab parties than to accept a government with Netanyahu and his political partners.
They also question why Eisenkot would need to join the coalition if a security escalation with Iran occurred. He could instead follow Liberman's approach after October 7 and support the government from outside the coalition without formally joining it.
"As long as his voters oppose joining Netanyahu, Eisenkot will not go against their wishes," political sources estimate.
Liberman cuts contact with opposition leaders
In a separate development, N12 News reported on Wednesday that Liberman had cut off contact with Eisenkot and Bennett and had not answered calls from opposition counterparts since the day after the election.
Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu party is currently projected to win seven Knesset seats, below pre-election polls that had suggested it could secure as many as nine.
According to N12, Liberman lost ground to Bennett, whose B'Yachad party absorbed some of his mandates. His election strategy had also relied on Likud fracturing internally, but official results show the party retaining its position as the largest faction in the Knesset.
Liberman had launched his campaign with the ambition of becoming prime minister, but fell short. Despite his reported shift towards a unity government, he has remained adamant in his refusal to join Netanyahu's coalition.
His opposition to Netanyahu was also evident in his recent call for Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara to open a criminal investigation into the prime minister. Liberman alleged that Netanyahu had attempted to draw the IDF into a military confrontation to delay the election.
According to N12, Liberman does not intend to be the one to cross over to Netanyahu's bloc and allegedly prefers that Eisenkot do so alone.
Sources close to Liberman told N12 that he is "choosing to lie in wait", as a security escalation could create further opportunities for political realignment.
Netanyahu's options depend on final results
Netanyahu's associates believe recruiting opposition lawmakers could become a simpler route to forming a government if his bloc approaches 60 Knesset seats. Likud officials claim they have already identified potential candidates who could be persuaded to cross political lines.
However, the final results remain pending, and there is no indication that Eisenkot is prepared to join Netanyahu or accept either proposed arrangement.
The central question is whether Netanyahu can secure enough support to govern without relying solely on his existing right-wing and ultra-Orthodox allies. The opposition, meanwhile, faces the challenge of maintaining unity as leaders reassess their options following the election.

How the Powerlist is chosen
Bharat Makers honours the people who keep that promise with their own hands.

- The people Doers from every walk Founders and farmers, teachers and nurses, artisans, creators, officers and volunteers.

Leaders from enterprise, public health, education, social impact, climate and rural development, and media and culture. Members recuse themselves from any category where a conflict exists. The full jury will be announced in November 2026.

Yes. title: Andre Agassi bought a Las Vegas land parcel for $6.5 million in 2018 and sold it for $18.15 million in 2026
raw_text:
Earlier this year, tennis legend Andre Agassi turned a piece of prime Las Vegas real estate into an $18.15 million payday. The 55-year-old former champion sold a vacant 1.8-acre homesite in the exclusive Summit Club community, earning nearly three times what he paid for the property in 2018. The deal offers a glimpse into the value of luxury land in Summerlin, where privacy, sweeping views and high-end amenities attract wealthy buyers. Yet the sale also reflects a personal change for Agassi, who reportedly reconsidered his plans for a sprawling family home as he moves towards a new stage of life.
Andre Agassi earns $11.65 million from his Las Vegas property sale
Andre Agassi purchased the land for $6.5 million in 2018, according to property records cited by the 
Las Vegas Review-Journal
. Its sale for $18.15 million represents a gain of $11.65 million before taxes, fees and other costs. The price highlights the appeal of the Summit Club, a guard-gated luxury community in Summerlin known for its large estates and exclusive facilities.
The 1.8-acre parcel sits on the western edge of the Las Vegas Valley. Its elevated position offers broad views of the city and surrounding mountains, making it an attractive site for a custom-built mansion. The community also features an 18-hole golf course, a luxury clubhouse and an outdoor team that helps residents explore the region.
Despite the property's potential, Agassi never filed development plans for the site, according to Clark County records. His brother and listing agent, Phillip Agassi, said the tennis star had initially considered building a large home there. However, with his children growing older, downsizing became a more practical choice.
The sale also stands out because the buyer's identity remains undisclosed. The purchase closed in February 2026 through a series of limited-liability companies, making it difficult to establish who ultimately acquired the land.
Andre Agassi's Summit Club sale highlights luxury real estate demand
Andre Agassi's property deal adds to the appeal of Summerlin, a master-planned community that has attracted affluent residents, including actor Mark Wahlberg. The Summit Club's privacy and extensive security measures help distinguish it from other luxury developments in the Las Vegas area.
Tyler Brady, owner of Brady Luxury Homes, highlighted the community's security, saying, “You’re not getting into the Summit and not getting caught,” he said.
Agassi built his fortune through a remarkable tennis career, winning eight major singles titles and an Olympic gold medal. He also earned more than $31 million in career prize money, while his wife, Steffi Graf, remains one of the sport's most celebrated champions.
The $18.15 million sale shows how valuable a well-positioned piece of land can become in a sought-after luxury market. For Agassi, it also closes the chapter on a property he once planned to turn into a family home.

title: Stephen Curry celebrates wife Ayesha’s career first as her latest move takes her beyond the kitchen and into holiday movies
raw_text:
Ayesha Curry
 has her first leading role in a feature film, and her husband was quick to react. Roku released the trailer and premiere date for “Second Chance Holiday” on Tuesday, October 27, almost four months after naming her the headliner in July. Stephen Curry posted his response on Instagram once the news was out. The holiday romantic comedy casts her as a dating expert opposite Matthew Daddario. It starts streaming on the Roku Channel on November 5.
Stephen Curry backs Ayesha Curry’s first leading film role
Stephen Curry marked the moment on Instagram Stories with a short greeting for Ayesha: “My Leading Lady.” He wrote that he sees the work behind the scenes, and that the public now gets to watch her shine. The Golden State Warriors star added that this is only the beginning.
Ayesha plays Chelsey Banks, a dating expert who keeps getting dumped around the holidays. She goes home for a fresh start and runs into her high school sweetheart, played by Daddario. Roku describes her streak as a possible curse, or maybe the universe nudging her back to her first love.
Maxwell McGuire directs from a script by Erin Muroski. Muse Entertainment produced the film with Motion Entertainment. Dennis Andres and Arlene Duncan co-star, and viewers can stream it free.
Ayesha said in a July statement she “fell in love with” Chelsey while bringing her to life.
Ayesha Curry’s acting credits before the lead role
Acting is not new to her. Ayesha landed small parts as a child actor on Hannah Montana and Good Luck Charlie, then turned up later in Ballers and A Black Lady Sketch Show. Netflix’s Irish Wish put her opposite 
Lindsay Lohan
 in 2024. Last year she played a TV host in Hulu’s Joy to the World, a supporting turn in another holiday comedy.
The top billing is what changes this time. Until now, she had never carried a feature film.
GOAT, an animated film, premiered in February. Curry produced it and appeared in it, while Ayesha voiced Carol, the manager of Whiskers Diner.
The couple also share a Broadway credit. They co-produced “The Lost Boys: A New Musical,” which opened April 26 and picked up 12 Tony nominations. Their arts projects run through Unanimous Media, the production company Curry owns. Now, Ayesha is expanding her resume with standout titles alongside her business ventures and she certainly has her husband Steph's unwavering support.

SUMMARY
Netanyahu's Likud emerges as the biggest party as counting concludes for Israel elections, a day after the country voted in parliamentary elections on October 27. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking an unprecedented seventh term amid public scrutiny of his government's handling of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack, the wars that followed and a series of domestic and foreign policy challenges. The election is shaping up as a crucial test of Netanyahu's leadership, with opposition figures, including former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and former prime minister Naftali Bennett, seeking to unseat his right-wing coalition. 
Netanyahu has claimed a “clear, decisive majority” for his right-wing bloc and called for a strong national government, even as exit polls projected a deadlock that could leave Arab-led parties holding the balance of power. Addressing supporters at Likud’s election headquarters in Jerusalem, Netanyahu said his party remained Israel’s largest political force and insisted the right-wing camp had enough support to govern. 
Netanyahu rejected relying on Arab-led parties, describing them as “against our existence”, and called for a “national right-wing government”. He also said Israel was facing a historic opportunity alongside US President Donald Trump to “remove the Iranian threat once and for all”. 
However, with 90% of votes counted, Netanyahu's party is set to have 51 seats, Eisenkot’s 48 while Arab parties are set to be kingmakers with 19 seats. 
Celebrations erupted in Lod, Kafr Manda and Tayibe following the projections for the Joint Arab List and United Arab List. Eisenkot said the results reflected a “lack of confidence” in Netanyahu and declared that voters had chosen change. He promised “a new era — an era of hope” and warned Netanyahu against using Israel’s security for political purposes while serving as caretaker prime minister. 
Turnout exceeded 77 per cent, the highest since 1999. Neither bloc appeared to have secured the 61 seats required for a majority, leaving coalition negotiations and the final count crucial to determining Israel’s next government.

08:20 (IST) Oct 29
Arab parties claim kingmaker status in Israel
Israel's Arab parties appear to secure a record number of seats in parliament and could emerge as kingmakers after strong turnout in Tuesday's election. Vote tallies show the two main Arab parties on course to win around 19 seats, nearly double their current representation in the Knesset. The two main parties are Yousef Jabareen-led Joint List and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas. Read full story
07:52 (IST) Oct 29
Hundreds protest in Israel, call for Jewish-Arab government
Around 300 protesters gathered in Jerusalem, Tel Aviv and Haifa demanding a Jewish-Arab government as partial election results showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc leading with 53 seats. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot vowed to push for a change in government, while Yair Golan said he would hold talks with party leaders on coalition formation. Eisenkot said the results showed “no confidence in the government of October 7 and draft evasion”.
06:51 (IST) Oct 29
No clear winner in Israel election with nearly 90% counted; Netanyahu bloc at 53, opposition at 48
No clear winner has emerged from Israel's election, with nearly 90% of ballots counted and both major political blocs falling short of the 61 seats needed to form a government.
The Israeli Central Elections Committee said it had counted more than five million votes as of 9 pm local time. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc is on course to win 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot is expected to secure 48.
05:46 (IST) Oct 29
Trump takes credit for Netanyahu's poll performance, says he'll "take a look" at coalition talks
US President Donald Trump on Wednesday took credit for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s performance in the country’s closely contested election, asserting that his public backing enhanced the incumbent leader’s prospects.
Trump additionally remarked that he would contemplate participating in endeavours aimed at establishing a unity government within Israel. During a conversation with Axios on Wednesday, Trump observed that Netanyahu was in a favourable position after partial results showed his political bloc leading ahead of the opposition, notwithstanding the fact that neither faction appeared to have achieved an outright parliamentary majority.
“I heard my endorsement made a big difference for Bibi,” Trump stated, employing the prime minister’s familiar moniker. When queried regarding whether he would assist with efforts to form a unity government headed by Netanyahu, Trump responded, “I will take a look.”
04:44 (IST) Oct 29
Counting of ‘double envelope’ votes has begun, says Israel's Central Elections Commission
The Central Elections Commission announces that the counting of the “double envelope” votes has now begun.
The double envelopes represent the voters who cast absentee ballots, largely made up of IDF soldiers, along with votes from prisoners, medical personnel, those with medical conditions, and Israeli representatives in missions abroad.
The CEC also notes that the counting of all of the regular votes has not completely finished. It says that results have been processed from 11,712 out of the 12,018 regular polling stations, representing 5,126,759 voters. The remaining polling stations are currently undergoing standard verification procedures, it adds.
03:11 (IST) Oct 29
Joint List reiterates it’s ready for ‘political cooperation to oust the Netanyahu government’
In a statement, the Arab-led Joint List party says it’s ready for “political cooperation to oust the Netanyahu government.”
The Joint List is projected to win 12 seats, making it tied for the third-biggest party in the Knesset, but most Jewish-led opposition parties have ruled out partnering with it to form a coalition.
“Our public understands the significance of the moment and went in droves to the polls,” the party says. “The Joint List will work with all its strength to bring an end to Netanyahu’s rule. We are ready for political cooperation to establish an alternative government, which will present a true alternative and commit itself to a true change of the current government’s racist policy.”
Earlier, Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen told Channel 13, “Anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu’s government of bloodshed will have to talk to us in order to pave the way for the change that the Israeli public longs for.”
22:34 (IST) Oct 28
Netanyahu accuses Arab parties of 'stealing' elections
21:37 (IST) Oct 28
Joint List chief Yousef Jabareen vows to help oust Netanyahu, calls for Jewish-Arab alliance
Yousef Jabareen, chairman of Israel's Arab-majority Joint List alliance, issued a sharp response following the conclusion of voting in the Israeli general election, declaring his party's readiness to clear the path for removing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from power.
In a public statement posted on social media, Jabareen framed the election outcome as a critical juncture for Israeli democracy, strongly condemning the policies of the governing coalition while presenting a joint Arab-Jewish alliance as the country's true path forward.
"We are ready and prepared to pave the way for the ousting of the Netanyahu government," Jabareen stated. "Against a government of bloodshed, against a politics of supremacy, racism, and exclusion, we offer a completely different alternative."
Rejecting the nationalist direction of the incumbent government, Jabareen emphasised that genuine political reform must be anchored in shared governance and equality across both communities.
"The change comes through Jewish-Arab partnership, a true and equal partnership," Jabareen declared. "No less than that, and no more than that."
20:57 (IST) Oct 28
Israel President Herzog urges parties to keep ‘open mind’ during government formation talks
Israeli President Isaac Herzog urged party leaders to come together with an open mind following Tuesday's general election, emphasising that political leaders must make every effort to avoid dragging the country into another round of elections.
"I will receive the official results next week," Herzog explained. "We will wait for the official election results next week; Justice Sohlberg will present the official results to me. After that, I will begin the consultation process here. I will listen to each and every faction, ask questions, and hold discussions."
"One thing must be understood, and I already said this before the elections: everything must be done, certainly after yesterday, not to return to another round of elections," Herzog warned. "And I expect everyone who comes here to arrive with an open mind."
20:45 (IST) Oct 28
Arab parties make historic gains, but Netanyahu’s rivals face coalition dilemma
Arab-led parties made a historic showing, but it’s not clear if the other opponents of Netanyahu's far-right government would form a coalition with them for a majority of seats in parliament.
His top challenger, centrist former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, has left the door open to partnering with Arab parties under certain conditions, including their recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and of Hamas as an extremist group.
It's not clear whether some of Eisenkot's likely partners who have ruled out such an alliance will change their minds to force Netanyahu from office.
Israeli voters choose parties, not individuals. With 85% of votes counted, Netanyahu’s Likud party has 20.8% and Eisenkot's Yashar party has 16.1%. Arab-led parties had 14.9%.
20:23 (IST) Oct 28
Trump hopes for Israeli coalition without far-right ministers Ben-Gvir, Smotrich: Report
US President Donald Trump hopes to see an Israeli governing coalition formed without right-wing ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.
The Jerusalem Post reported on Wednesday, citing news outlet Walla, that American sources indicated that Trump views settler violence as a direct obstacle to implementing his broader regional strategy.
While Trump's advisors have been briefed on the initial exit poll results following the Israeli elections, the US president has not yet offered official public comments regarding the outcome.
19:18 (IST) Oct 28
Netanyahu-led bloc at 53 seats, Eisenkot's coalition at 48 after 85% votes counted
The Central Elections Committee announces 53 seats for the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and 48 seats for the bloc led by Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot.
The Arab parties have 19 seats, a historic high.
18:59 (IST) Oct 28
Voting over, counting under way: What happens next in Israel’s election
Vote counting is underway in Israel following the October 27 parliamentary elections, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc appearing on course to emerge as the largest in the 120-member Knesset.
However, neither Netanyahu’s coalition nor the opposition alliance led by Yashar party chief and former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, who has emerged as the Israeli premier's main rival, is likely to secure a clear majority.
Once the final results are declared, parties are expected to engage in potentially lengthy negotiations to form a governing coalition. If the talks fail, Israel could face another election.
Read full story
18:41 (IST) Oct 28
Who is Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main challenger
Gadi Eisenkot, a former chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces (IDF), challenged Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with a campaign centred on security, leadership and accountability for the failures surrounding Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack.
Eisenkot, who founded the Yashar party in 2025, emerged as a key challenger to Netanyahu for Israel's October 27 election.
Unlike Netanyahu, a veteran and combative politician, Eisenkot has cultivated an image of a reserved, straightforward leader with strong military credentials. His family has also suffered personal losses during the Gaza war, with his son and two nephews killed while fighting there.
Read full story
18:30 (IST) Oct 28
Netanyahu warns against left-wing govt after Joint List ally calls Jerusalem 'occupied'
17:47 (IST) Oct 28
Netanyahu-led Likud bloc as counting of votes underway
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies appear on track to win the most seats in Israel's parliament after an election this week, though neither he nor his main competitor, Gadi Eisenkot, has a clear path to a majority.
Votes are now being tallied, followed by potentially long negotiations as parties try to assemble a governing coalition. If those talks fail, Israel could head to another round of elections.
17:08 (IST) Oct 28
84% votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc ahead by just five seats
With 84.5% of ballot boxes counted as of 12:34 pm local time, partial results published by Israel's Central Elections Committee gave 54 seats to the bloc led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and 49 seats to the bloc led by Yashar’s Gadi Eisenkot, The Times of Israel reported.
16:42 (IST) Oct 28
'We changed fate of Middle East': Netanyahu thanks supporters
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared Likud the largest party in parliament as initial vote tallies emerged, saying his government’s military actions had “changed the face of the Middle East” and calling for the formation of a strong right-wing government.
Addressing supporters at Likud’s election headquarters, Netanyahu cited military operations against Hamas, Hezbollah and Iran, claiming they had strengthened Israel’s security. However, he warned that the threat from Tehran remained as long as its current regime stayed in power.
He also claimed that the broader right-wing bloc had secured a decisive majority among Jewish and Zionist voters, urging nationalist parties to unite behind a coalition. Netanyahu criticised opposition leaders for considering alliances with Arab-led parties, arguing that such a government would endanger Israel’s security.
Netanyahu thanked voters, Israeli soldiers and his family, and said Israel faced a historic opportunity, alongside US President Donald Trump, to eliminate the threat from Iran.
16:36 (IST) Oct 28
Far-left candidate calls for 'genuine Jewish-Arab partnership' to unseat Netanyahu
The leader of one of Israel's Arab-majority lists, which are projected to make strong gains in close-fought elections, called on Wednesday for a "genuine Jewish-Arab partnership" to help remove Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"Anyone who wants to offer a substantive and genuine alternative to Netanyahu's blood-soaked government will have to talk to us to secure the path to the change that the public in Israel longs for," Yousef Jabareen, who heads the far-left Joint List, told Israeli media.
15:50 (IST) Oct 28
Why forming a government in Israel could take weeks after the election results
After the final tally is in, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders on whom they want as prime minister and then tap the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming a government.
That nominee has up to 42 days to form a government.
No single party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, so governments are formed by a coalition of parties, and negotiations on forming a government often take weeks. Every Knesset seat counts and small parties can have a big impact by becoming kingmakers.
If the nominee fails, others can get a chance to try. If no government emerges, another election is called, with the present cabinet staying on as a caretaker government.

title: 'Garam paani piyo, thanda mat peena': Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's reaction to fan goes viral - WATCH
raw_text:
Whether it is his innocence or his blistering batting, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has become a fan favourite. At just 15, Sooryavanshi is taking on international bowlers without fear. He can smash sixes, score runs at a stunning pace and put opposition attacks under pressure. Yet, away from the cricket field, he is still a young boy who brings out the protective side of people around him.
A recent video from Wellington, New Zealand, shows exactly why the teenager has become a fan favourite in such a short time.
After India's third T20I against New Zealand, Sooryavanshi went near the boundary to sign autographs for fans. As he interacted with the crowd, a woman called out to him from the stands.
“Vaibhav… hum log bhi Ballia se hain. Kaise ho, theek ho? Garam paani piyo, thanda mat peena [Vaibhav, we are also from Ballia. How are you? Are you fine? Drink warm water, don't drink cold water],” she said.
Sooryavanshi smiled and then continued signing autographs for his fans.
The brief exchange has gone viral on social media.
Fearless with the bat, innocent off the field
Sooryavanshi's rise has been nothing short of remarkable.

At the other end, 
Abhishek Sharma
 played a sensational knock of 113 off 38 balls. The opening pair added 133 runs in just 7.1 overs as India reached the target in 13.2 overs, winning by six wickets and taking an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.

 after the match, Abhishek revealed that Sooryavanshi had spoken about playing fearlessly during their net session.
“Yesterday, Vaibhav told me something in the nets that I will play the same way as in the Milkha Singh movie Bhag Milkha Bhag dialogue ‘Bhaiya, khelunga bhi waise hi’,” Abhishek said.
The line, inspired by the Bollywood film Bhaag Milkha Bhaag, means, “Brother, I will play the same way.”
Sooryavanshi backed up those words with his performance against New Zealand. Abhishek said the youngster's aggressive start also gave confidence to the batter at the other end.
“When you are chasing 200 or 190, his first ball, first over, is his main fast baller. And if you show such aggression as an opener. Because I was on the other side, so I saw that. On the first ball, the non-striker gets excited,” Abhishek said.

title: 68 killed in Spain train collision: Videos capture overturned carriages, injured passengers, devastation
raw_text:
At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spain’s central province of Toledo. Videos and photographs from the scene showed overturned carriages, injured passengers and emergency crews working to rescue people trapped in the wreckage.
The collision occurred on Wednesday morning near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville rail route. Recordings captured by passengers showed scenes inside the trains following the impact, while images from the site showed carriages lying on their sides beside the tracks.
Emergency services rushed to the scene to evacuate passengers, provide medical assistance and search the wreckage for survivors. Injured passengers were taken to nearby medical facilities, including a sports centre converted into a temporary treatment site. The regional government of Castilla-La Mancha said 58 people were receiving treatment in hospitals.
According to Spain’s rail infrastructure operator ADIF, both trains were travelling south from Madrid towards Seville when the collision occurred. A state-owned RENFE train struck the rear of an IRYO train that had stopped on the tracks, derailing carriages on both trains.
Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente said a failure in the railway’s computer communications system had disrupted safety operations before the collision. The malfunction automatically stopped trains along a 63-kilometre stretch of track, after which the RENFE train was reportedly allowed to proceed despite a red signal.
According to accounts of the incident, ADIF took manual control of the system following the failure. Puente said the train was authorised to continue under circumstances that investigators would need to examine.
“There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed,” Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday. “It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.”
The RENFE train reportedly resumed its journey at about 124 miles per hour before hitting the stationary IRYO train. Authorities have yet to establish the full sequence of events leading to the crash.
Meanwhile, Spanish trade union CSIF has demanded the resignation of the transport minister following the collision. The union accused Puente of shifting responsibility onto a railway official rather than accepting accountability for the disaster. Anger over the crash spilled onto the streets of Madrid on Wednesday night, when around 500 demonstrators gathered outside the Transport Ministry. Some protesters threw bottles and flares at police, prompting officers to deploy tear gas to disperse the crowd, Reuters reported.
The disaster comes after another deadly rail collision in Spain earlier this year. A January crash in Córdoba province killed more than 40 people, while a separate incident near Barcelona claimed the life of a train driver.
Rescue teams continued searching the damaged carriages as authorities worked to identify victims, assist survivors and establish the cause of the collision. Investigators are expected to examine the signalling system, communications failure and the decision to allow the train to proceed despite the red signal.

title: Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce’s $200 million Garage Beer rides a 252% sales boom, but a 14-million-barrel rival poses a major challenge
raw_text:
The American beer market has become a tough place for smaller brands, but Garage Beer is finding room to grow. Backed by NFL stars Jason and 
Travis Kelce
, the light beer brand has expanded beyond its Midwestern roots and built a national presence. Its rise is not just about celebrity ownership. A simple product, sharp marketing and a clear understanding of everyday drinkers have helped Garage Beer stand out. With sales climbing and distribution reaching all 50 states, the company is taking on established beer giants in a category where winning shelf space is never easy.
Garage Beer sales surge as the Kelce brothers expand their reach
Garage Beer recorded a remarkable 252% sales increase in 2023, before the Kelce brothers became majority investors in 2024. That timeline matters because it shows the brand had already gained traction before its biggest celebrity boost arrived.
The beer began as a product from Braxton Brewing Company in Kentucky. Its relaunch in early 2023 gave it a fresh identity, with a lighter recipe, new packaging and a focus on just 95 calories per serving. Instead of competing for attention among specialist craft beers, Garage Beer targeted drinkers who wanted an easygoing alternative to mainstream lagers.
The Kelce brothers then brought their enormous fan bases and marketing appeal into the picture. Jason's entertaining social media videos, creative promotions and unusual partnerships helped the brand earn attention without relying entirely on traditional advertising.
Garage Beer CEO Andy Sauer explained the thinking behind its approach: “I wanted people who were willing to take risks, people who were willing to do something different,” he says. “That’s one of the more monolithic categories in all of grocery. You need people who are comfortable with the idea of very different thinking.”
That willingness to experiment has helped Garage Beer build a personality beyond its product. It has also given the brand a way to compete against companies with much larger advertising budgets.
Garage Beer faces a bigger test against established beer giants
National distribution marks a major milestone, but sustaining growth could prove harder than securing attention. Garage Beer is entering a market dominated by established names such as Michelob Ultra, Busch Light and Modelo Especial..
The scale of that competition is clear. According to the figures cited by VinePair, Garage Beer expected to produce around 300,000 barrels in 2025. Michelob Ultra, meanwhile, held an 8.2% share of the US beer market by volume, illustrating the gap between a rising challenger and an industry heavyweight.
The Kelce brothers provide a valuable advantage, but long-term success will depend on repeat purchases, reliable distribution and keeping consumers interested after the initial excitement fades.
Production has also moved beyond Braxton Brewing Company to include partners such as Founders Brewing Co., allowing Garage Beer to meet growing demand.
For now, Garage Beer has shown that a smaller brand can challenge established players with a focused product and memorable marketing. The bigger question is whether it can turn celebrity-driven attention into lasting consumer loyalty.

title: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current make history as 18,000 fans turn final home game into a record-breaking event
raw_text:
Patrick Mahomes
 and 
Brittany Mahomes
 have another reason to celebrate their investment in Kansas City sports. The Kansas City Current drew a record-setting crowd for their final home match of the 2026 season, turning the occasion into more than a football game. With thousands of supporters gathering outside CPKC Stadium, the club expanded its matchday experience and brought more fans into the celebration. The milestone also highlighted the growing appeal of women's soccer in Kansas City, where the Mahomes family's involvement in the Current has become part of a wider push to build a strong sporting community..
Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current welcome a record crowd
The Kansas City Current made history on October 25, welcoming a crowd expected to reach around 18,000 for the club's biggest-attended match. With CPKC Stadium holding about 12,000 people, the team introduced a new Ground Pass experience at Current Landing to give more supporters a place to watch the action..
Around 6,000 fans gathered in the outdoor area, where large screens, food, games and family-friendly activities created a festival-like atmosphere. The $10 pass offered access to five viewing screens, a children's zone and halftime entertainment, giving fans another way to take part even if they could not secure stadium tickets.
Jocelyn Monroe, the club's chief marketing director, said the occasion was about bringing the city together.
“It’s a fun day to come out and celebrate Kansas City and celebrate sports in Kansas City and be a part of history because this will be our largest attended match in Kansas City Current history,” said Jocelyn Monroe, chief marketing director of KC Current.
The club also stressed the importance of making its matches accessible to more people.
“What really makes the atmosphere is the people, so having more of our fans have the opportunity to come down and build out an accessible area for them is something we always were thinking about,” Monroe said.
For Patrick and Brittany Mahomes, who are part of the ownership group behind the KC Current, the milestone reflects the team's growing reach beyond the pitch. The turnout also showed how a match can become a citywide event rather than an experience limited to those inside the stadium..
KC Current expands Current Landing with new restaurants and events
The celebration brought fresh activity to Current Landing, the entertainment district surrounding the stadium. Two dining options, Revel Bar & Grill and Providence Pizza, added to the area's appeal on an already busy matchday.
Providence Pizza marked its grand opening on Sunday, with owner Aaron acknowledging both the excitement and the challenge of opening on such a busy day.
“We are excited and nervous. This is our grand opening, so we are opening our restaurant on one of the probably busiest days for Current Landing,” said Aaron, the owner of Providence Pizza..
The Current plans to build on the success by hosting more One Current events at Current Landing throughout the year. These gatherings could give supporters more chances to connect with the team outside regular matchdays.
For the Mahomes-backed club, the record crowd offers a clear sign of growing fan interest. By combining soccer, food and entertainment, the Current is working to make its home ground a destination for the wider Kansas City community.
